title: On Windows, cron jobs silently run inside WSL instead of a real shell, because Bun.which("bash") finds WSL's launcher stub first
body:
## Summary

Every Pulse cron job that shells out via `spawnScript()` in `PULSE/lib.ts` silently fails on Windows, forever, with no error surfaced anywhere except `consecutiveFailures` climbing in `state.json` and `healthz` eventually reporting `"degraded"`.

**Environment:** Windows 10 Pro with WSL installed (a very common combination — WSL ships by default on modern Windows and many dev machines have it enabled), Bun 1.3.10.

## Root cause

`lib.ts` resolves the shell once, at module load:

```ts
const BASH_PATH = Bun.which("bash") ?? "/bin/bash"
```

and then spawns every job with `Bun.spawn([BASH_PATH, "-c", command], ...)`.

On Windows, `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` is a launcher stub for WSL, and System32 sits ahead of Git for Windows' install directories in the default PATH. So `Bun.which("bash")` resolves to the WSL stub, not a real POSIX shell in the host environment. Spawning it launches an entire separate Linux VM (whatever the default WSL distro is) with its own filesystem and PATH, completely disconnected from the Windows install — `bun` isn't installed there, so every job dies with `bun: command not found`, and that error goes into the job's captured stderr, which is only ever logged, never surfaced as a startup-time warning.

## Repro

```powershell
# In a PowerShell session with the default Windows PATH (System32 before
# any Git for Windows directories):
bun -e "console.log(Bun.which('bash'))"
# -> C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe   (WSL, not a real shell)

# Confirm the collision directly:
& "C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe" -c "bun --version"
# -> /bin/bash: line 1: bun: command not found
```

Any Pulse job defined with `type = "script"` in `PULSE.toml` fails this way, invisibly, from the very first tick.

## Fix

Resolve the shell more carefully on Windows: probe Git for Windows' actual `bash.exe` locations first (`Git\bin\bash.exe`, then `Git\usr\bin\bash.exe`), and only fall back to `Bun.which("bash")` (still useful on macOS/Linux, where there's no WSL-style collision) if neither is found.

```ts
const BASH_PATH =
  (process.platform === "win32"
    ? [
        join(process.env.ProgramFiles ?? "C:\\Program Files", "Git", "bin", "bash.exe"),
        join(process.env.ProgramFiles ?? "C:\\Program Files", "Git", "usr", "bin", "bash.exe"),
      ].find((p) => existsSync(p))
    : undefined) ??
  Bun.which("bash") ??
  "/bin/bash"
```

## Testing performed

Verified via `PULSE/run-job.ts <job-name>` (invokes the exact same `spawnScript()` path the cron loop uses) — both of this install's script-type jobs, which had been failing on every tick, now exit 0 and produce their expected output.

## Related

Same Windows Pulse work that turned up #2222, #2223, #2224 — this one is in core `lib.ts` rather than the Windows-port-specific `manage.ps1`/`PulseStart.ps1`, so it likely affects any Windows install with WSL present, not just this port.

comments.body: Related: #2222, #2223, #2224 (same Windows Pulse work, found while getting Pulse fully running end to end on Windows).

Scoping data point: installs that run Pulse under Linux Bun inside WSL2 aren't affected. `Bun.which("bash")` resolves to the distro's own `/usr/bin/bash`, so the System32 stub never comes into play. The failure is specific to Windows-native Bun, not any Windows install with WSL present. The `win32` guard in the proposed fix is a no-op elsewhere, so it looks safe to merge for native-Windows users.

Thanks @aveneri, and @garthsch for scoping it to native-Windows Bun. On Windows, `PULSE/lib.ts` now looks for Git for Windows' `bash.exe` before falling back to `Bun.which("bash")`, so jobs no longer land in WSL's launcher. The check only runs on win32. Next release carries it.

Your own `mountinfo` output has the answer, and it isn't Hermes:

```
/proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:1716 - proc proc rw,hidepid=invisible,subset=pid
```

`subset=pid` is a **kernel proc mount option**. When it's set, `/proc` exposes only the per-PID directories and hides every non-process file — which is exactly `/proc/uptime`, `/proc/meminfo`, and `/proc/loadavg`, i.e. precisely what `uptime` and `free -h` read. That's why your listing shows only numeric PID dirs. `hidepid=invisible` additionally hides other users' PIDs.

Note the line immediately above it in your paste:

```
/ /dev/.lxc/proc rw,relatime shared:1583 master:1385 - proc proc rw
```

That `/dev/.lxc/` path is the container runtime's own proc handling — the restricted `/proc` is being mounted by your **LXC container config**, not by the agent.

Hermes does not set these options. I grepped the tree for every mechanism that could: `hidepid`, `subset=pid`, systemd's `ProtectProc=` / `ProcSubset=`, and any private-mount setup. The only match anywhere is a comment in `hermes_state.py` that *reads* `/proc` defensively and notes a hidepid mount as one reason a PID lookup can fail. There is no code path that mounts or remounts `/proc`, and subprocesses are spawned in the same mount namespace as the agent — there is no per-subprocess isolation to disable, which is why you couldn't find a setting for it in the docs.

The v0.21.0 timing is almost certainly coincidental with a container-runtime or host change

There is no setting for this because Hermes does not isolate /proc for its subprocesses: the gateway unit it generates (hermes_cli/gateway.py:3282) has no ProtectProc/ProcSubset/PrivateMounts directives, and there is no mount-namespace code in any spawn path — subprocesses run in the service's own mount namespace. title: fix: no_agent cron .sh scripts fail on Windows — MSYS/Git bash mangles the backslash script path (exit 127 'No such file or directory')
body:
## Environment
- OS: Windows 10/11 (native, not WSL)
- Hermes Agent: gateway running under `hermes-agent` (scheduled task `Hermes_Gateway` -> `pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`)
- Shell tool backend: git-bash / MSYS
- Cron jobs: `no_agent: true`, `script: <name>.sh` (pre-run data-collection scripts)

## Summary
On Windows, any `no_agent` cron job whose `script` is a `.sh` file fails with exit code 127. The scheduler resolves the script to a native Windows path (`C:\Users\...\script.sh`) and passes it as an argv element to the MSYS/Git bash it finds via `shutil.which("bash")`. MSYS bash converts/strips the backslashes in that argv, producing `C:Userslymes...AppDataLocalhermesscriptsscript.sh` — which cannot be opened, so bash exits 127 with `No such file or directory`.

This breaks *all* `.sh` `no_agent` crons on Windows. It is reproducible for both scheduled ticks and manual `hermes cron run <id>`.

## Reproduction
1. On Windows, create a cron with a `.sh` script and `no_agent: true`:
   ```bash
   hermes cron create "every 6h" --script o2b-index.sh --no-agent
   ```
2. Trigger it: `hermes cron run <id>` (or wait for the tick).
3. Observe `last_status: error` with:
   ```
   Script exited with code 127
   stderr:
   /bin/bash: C:UserslymesAppDataLocalhermesscriptso2b-index.sh: No such file or directory
   ```

## Expected
The cron runs the `.sh` script successfully (exit 0), the same way it does on Linux/macOS.

## Actual
`Script exited with code 127` — bash cannot find the script because the backslash path was mangled by MSYS argv conversion.

## Root cause
In `cron/scheduler.py`, `_run_job_script()` builds the subprocess argv as:

```python
_bash = shutil.which("bash")          # -> ...\hermes\git\usr\bin\bash.EXE  (MSYS bash)
argv = [_bash, str(path)]              # str(path) = "C:\Users\...\script.sh"
```

The resolved `path` is a native Windows path with backslashes. MSYS/Git bash applies path conversion to argv elements that look like Windows paths, converting `C:\Users\...\script.sh` into `C:Users\...` (backslashes dropped, drive colon stripped). The script is never launched.

The scheduler already sets `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` / `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*` in the child env (`tools/environments/local.py`), but this does **not** prevent the mangling for the bash binary it selects — so that mitigation is ineffective for this code path.

## Evidence
Captured argv actually constructed by the code (bash + script arg):

```
['C:\\Users\\lymes\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\git\\usr\\bin\\bash.EXE',
 'C:\\Users\\lymes\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\scripts\\o2b-dream.sh']   # before fix -> mangled by bash
```

When the same script arg is given in MSYS form, bash runs it fine (exit 0):

```
'/c/Users/lymes/AppData/Local/hermes/scripts/o2b-dream.sh'
```

Verified: `bash "/c/Users/.../o2b-dream.sh"` -> `rc=0` (both with and without `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV`).

## Suggested fix
Normalize the resolved script path to MSYS/POSIX form **before** constructing argv, in every branch that invokes the script — no `cygpath` dependency (the gateway's PATH may not include `git/usr/bin` where `cygpath` lives). Something like:

```python
argv = [_bash, str(path)]
if sys.platform == "win32":
    _wps = str(path)
    if _wps and ":" in _wps and "\\" in _wps:
        _drive, _rest = _wps.split(":", 1)
        _msys = "/" + _drive.lower() + _rest.replace("\\", "/")
        argv = [_bash, _msys]
```

This should be applied consistently across the scheduled-tick path **and** the manual `cron run` path (both ultimately route through `_run_job_script`, but the manual path should be confirmed to exercise the same normalization).

## Workaround (until fixed)
Wrap the `.sh` logic so it is invoked without a backslash path, e.g. call the script via an MSYS/POSIX path, or reimplement the job as a `.py` script (the non-`.sh` branch uses `sys.executable` and is unaffected).

## Related
- Affected jobs observed: `o2b-dream` (`every 1440m`, `no_agent`), `o2b-search-index` (`ever

title: [Bug]: After 'bun add -g omo-ai', ~/.bun/bin/omo needs node on PATH again (env: node: No such file or directory) until a node launch rewrites the bun shim
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I will write this issue in English
- [x] I have searched existing issues to avoid duplicates
- [ ] I am using the latest version of oh-my-openagent (5.1.4 installed; I checked that the relevant code is unchanged on `dev` / 5.1.5)
- [x] I have read the documentation

### Bug Description

After `bun add -g omo-ai` (the documented install/update line for package installs), `~/.bun/bin/omo` goes back to being bun's plain symlink to `bin/omo.js`, whose shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env node`. The "bun launcher shim" that execs bun directly is only written back by a launch that runs under node (`bin/lib/bun-bin-shim.js`: "Repairs run under node only").

So from the moment of the update until something launches `omo` under node, `omo` needs `node` on `PATH`. In an environment without node on `PATH` (a launchd job, cron, a bun-only machine, or node only through nvm), `omo` fails with `env: node: No such file or directory` (exit 127), and it cannot repair itself because the repair also needs node.

We hit this in a nightly launchd update script: `bun add -g omo-ai` succeeded, then the script's `omo --version` check printed nothing, and the script treated the update as broken. `omo` only worked again after it was launched from an interactive shell that had nvm's node on `PATH`.

### Steps to Reproduce

Isolated reproduction of the bun behavior (does not touch a real install):

```sh
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $T/pkg/bin
echo '{"name":"shimtest","version":"1.0.0","bin":{"shimtest":"bin/cli.js"}}' > $T/pkg/package.json
printf '#!/usr/bin/env node\nconsole.log("hi")\n' > $T/pkg/bin/cli.js; chmod +x $T/pkg/bin/cli.js
export BUN_INSTALL=$T/bun
bun add -g file:$T/pkg
# replace the link with a regular-file shim, as omo does
rm $T/bun/bin/shimtest; printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec bun "$@"\n' > $T/bun/bin/shimtest; chmod +x $T/bun/bin/shimtest
sed -i '' 's/1.0.0/1.0.1/' $T/pkg/package.json
bun add -g file:$T/pkg          # "update"
ls -la $T/bun/bin/shimtest      # symlink again
env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin $T/bun/bin/shimtest   # env: node: No such file or directory, exit 127
```

With omo itself:

1. Install omo with bun on a machine where `node` is only available through nvm (or not at all).
2. Launch `omo` once from a shell that has node, so the bun launcher shim is written.
3. Run `bun add -g omo-ai` (update).
4. Run `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/bin:/bin omo --version`.

### Expected Behavior

After a bun install or update, `omo` runs with bun alone, as the shim intends. For example, the shim could be written at install time, or the bun-global entry could avoid depending on `node` in its shebang.

### Actual Behavior

`env: node: No such file or directory`, exit 127, until `omo` is next launched under node.

### Doctor Output

```shell
PASS senpi version 2026.9.29-5
INFO omo · Edition: Native · Installed: 5.1.4 (engine: senpi 2026.9.29-5) · Latest: 5.1.5
INFO Update: bun add -g omo-ai
```
(trimmed to the version lines; the rest is per-session shard status)

### Error Logs

```shell
$ env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/omo-ai/bin/omo.js --version
env: node: No such file or directory

# nightly launchd update log (same PATH, 2026-09-30):
omo before: omo 5.1.1 (engine: senpi 2026.9.29)
... bun add -g omo-ai ...
omo after:
```

### Additional Context

- macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon
- omo 5.1.4 (engine: senpi 2026.9.29-5), installed with `bun add -g omo-ai`
- bun 1.4.2
- Running inside the herdr terminal multiplexer

`packages/omo-native/bin/lib/bun-bin-shim.js` and the `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang of `packages/omo-native/bin/omo.js` are identical on `dev`. The `postinstall` (`node bin/senpi-patch.mjs`) also assumes node.

### Operating System

macOS

comments.body:
Thank you @floweredao, a clear report, including the exact place the repair only happens under node.

We're taking it: after `bun add -g omo-ai`, `~/.bun/bin/omo` must keep working on a machine where `node` is not on `PATH` (a bun-only box, a launchd job, cron). The fix will either repair the shim from the bun path too, or ship a bin that is safe under bun from the start, with a test that runs the updated launcher on a node-less `PATH`. If you'd rather open the PR yourself, please do, and we'll review and land it instead.

Fixed by #9337, merged as afbb9c2412090ce815ca3837190599783fad299c. Cause: bun add -g restored Bun stock links to bin/omo.js, whose node shebang could not start when node was absent from PATH, while the launcher shim repair previously skipped Bun and therefore could not recover. RED/GREEN: on dev, the regression test left the bin as a symlink and a packed isolated Bun-only install exited 127 with env: node: No such file or directory; on the merged fix, Bun postinstall restored the shim, the same packed install produced a regular launcher and omo --version exited 0. Thank you @floweredao for the precise report and contribution.

title: Remove the orphaned /usr/local/lib/state-lib.sh from daniel-server
body:
## Problem

daniel-server still carries `/usr/local/lib/state-lib.sh` (root-owned, dated 2026-07-16). An earlier deploy of the Docker-era wg-easy role installed it there for the host cron `pull-pi-peers.sh`. That cron retired with the k3s migration, and #3748 deleted the repo source. Nothing on the host sources the file: a grep of `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/local/lib`, `/etc/cron.d`, `/etc/systemd/system` and `/var/spool/cron` finds only the file itself. daniel-pi has no copy.

The orphan is harmless. It misleads a reader who finds it on the host and searches the repo for its source.

## Fix

Delete it by hand on daniel-server: `sudo rm /usr/local/lib/state-lib.sh`. An agent session cannot, because the guard denies `sudo`. No Ansible task owns the path, so no absent-state task is needed.

ls /usr/local/lib/state-lib.sh on daniel-server reports No such file or directory.

Opening an existing session that was created by the Hermes desktop app and sending a message produces no reply and no error. The message never arrives on the desktop either. Reading the same conversation works normally, so the app looks connected and the chat looks healthy.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a session created by the desktop app (source `local`, id `local-<hash>`).
2. Open it in the app from the chat list.
3. Send any message.

### Expected

Either the message is delivered, or the app says why it cannot be.

### Actual

The app POSTs `/v1/chat/completions` with `X-Hermes-Session-Id: local-<hash>`; the gateway refuses the turn and delivers the refusal in-band inside **HTTP 200**, which the app does not surface:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions -> 200, 1,027 bytes

data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant"},"finish_reason":null}], ...}
data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"error"}],
       "error":{"message":"permission_denied","type":"RuntimeStoreError"},
       "hermes":{"completed":true,"partial":false,"failed":true,
                 "error":"permission_denied","error_code":"agent_error"}}
data: [DONE]
```

Server side the same failure logs as `Agent task chatcmpl-… failed during SSE streaming: permission_denied`, with no `inbound message` line — the turn never dispatches.

Same client, same server, session created by the app itself (`mob-…`): HTTP 200 with the actual answer (~62 KB in my test). Reads are unaffected in both cases — `GET /api/sessions/<local-id>/messages` returns 200 with the full history, which is why the conversation looks fine right up until you send.

### Cause

The gateway does not accept a turn submitted through the `api_server` platform into a session whose source is `local`, and returns that refusal as a completion error rather than an HTTP failure. The app lists such sessions without distinguishing them, offers them as chats, and then discards the error event.

### Why this is a bug rather than a request for a new capability

- The chat list is fully selectable, and selecting an existing session presents the composer. A UI that hands you a composer for a chat is asserting that the chat is writable.
- If resuming existing threads were not supported, the composer would not be presented for them. If either surface is the secondary one, it is the `+` new-chat control, not the existing-session list.
- It also worked previously. The refresh behaviour is a separate matter and is not part of this report: a phone must pull before it can even list a session started on the desktop, and after a desktop turn the phone needs a manual refresh to show it. Switching a conversation between desktop and mobile is not well served by either interface today — but on the path that matters here, the turn itself went through.

So the app offers a writable chat and then discards the server's refusal, leaving a message that appears sent and a conversation that never receives it.

### Suggested fixes — either one removes the silent failure

- Surface `finish_reason: "error"` / `hermes.failed: true` as a visible error in the chat and keep the draft, rather than ending the turn silently.
- Label or filter sessions the app cannot post into. `/api/sessions` returns a `source` field per session (`local`, `api_server`, `cron`, `subagent`, `tool`, …), verified against this server, so read-only sessions can be marked in the list.

### Environment

- App 2.1.33 (build 2176, versionCode 21762, arm64-v8a)
- Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 17
- Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24), gateway API server on :8642
- Reproduced first on 1.0.8 and again after a clean install of 2.1.33

title: os-sftp-backup: UI test fails with "Strict security" enabled, while cron backups work
body:
**Important notices**

Before you add a new report, we ask you kindly to acknowledge the following:

- [x] I have read the contributing guide lines at https://github.com/opnsense/plugins/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] I have searched the existing issues, open and closed, and I'm convinced that mine is new.
- [x] The title contains the plugin to which this issue belongs

**Describe the bug**

With "Strict security" enabled, the "Setup/Test sftp" function of os-sftp-backup fails with permission errors.

However, scheduled backups via cron work perfectly using the exact same configuration, SSH private key, and SFTP destination.

This strongly suggests that the UI-triggered operation runs with insufficient privileges, while the cron job executes successfully with the required permissions.

**To Reproduce**

1. Enable "Strict security" in OPNsense.
2. Configure os-sftp-backup with SSH key authentication.
3. Verify that scheduled cron backups complete successfully.
4. Open the SFTP backup configuration in the WebGUI.
5. Click "Setup/Test sftp".
6. Observe the permission errors.

**Expected behavior**

The UI-triggered SFTP test should work with "Strict security" enabled, just as scheduled cron backups do.

There should be no need to disable "Strict security" or weaken the permissions of the SSH private key.

**Screenshots**

Not applicable.

**Relevant log files**

The following errors are displayed in the WebGUI:

```text
The following input errors were detected:

Warning: Identity file /conf/backup/sftp/identity not accessible: Permission denied.
Could not create directory '/nonexistent/.ssh' (No such file or directory).
Failed to add the host to the list of known hosts (/nonexistent/.ssh/known_hosts).
opnsense@blob.mgsoft: Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
Connection closed
```

**Additional context**

The SSH key and remote SFTP configuration are known to be valid because scheduled cron backups succeed.

The likely cause is that the WebGUI invokes SFTP under an unprivileged account when "Strict security" is enabled:

- The private key at `/conf/backup/sftp/identity` cannot be read.
- The process uses `/nonexistent` as its home directory and cannot maintain `known_hosts`.
- Public key authentication consequently fails.

The UI operation should ideally use the same privileged backend execution mechanism as the scheduled cron backup.

This appears to be a compatibility issue between os-sftp-backup and OPNsense's "Strict security" mode, rather than an SSH configuration problem.

**Environment**

- OPNsense with "Strict security" enabled
- Plugin: os-sftp-backup
- Authentication: SSH public key
- Scheduled cron backups: working
- WebGUI "Setup/Test sftp": failing

title: Bug report: Redis persistence fails (Permission denied) + Ollama/qwen3 deriver integration issues
body:
### **Environment**

- honcho-aio: dub19/honcho-aio:latest (installed via Unraid Community Apps, host port 8001 → container 8000)
- Host: Unraid 6.x, 96 GB RAM, AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370
- Models: Ollama 0.33.3 (local), qwen3.5:35b for chat, nomic-embed-text:latest for embeddings (768 dims)

### **Bug 1: Redis cannot persist — Permission denied on every RDB save**
The bundled Redis is started by the s6 run script at /etc/services.d/redis/run:

`exec gosu redis redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6379`

No --dir is passed, so Redis falls back to its compiled-in default directory, /run/s6/legacy-services/redis, which is **owned by root** and not writable by the redis user. Every background save fails:

```
134:M 05 Sep 2026 14:46:46.429 # Failed opening the temp RDB file temp-134.rdb (in server root dir /run/s6/legacy-services/redis) for saving: Permission denied
134:M 05 Sep 2026 14:46:46.429 # Error trying to save the DB, can't exit.
Redis can also hang on shutdown because of this, which delays container stops.
```

The container bootstrap (/etc/cont-init.d/01-bootstrap.sh) already creates /data/redis (owned by redis:redis), clearly the intended location, but the run script never points Redis at it.

**Workaround (verified):** patch the run script to:

`exec gosu redis redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6379 --dir /data/redis`

After this, SAVE succeeds and dump.rdb is written into the persisted /mnt/user/appdata/honcho-aio/redis volume.

### **Bug 2: Deriver silently produces zero observations with qwen3 (Ollama)**
With CHAT_MODEL=local/qwen3.5:35b and default settings, the deriver fails on every work unit:

```
src.utils.json_parser - ERROR - ❌ Repair failed: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
src.deriver.deriver - WARNING - Deriver generated zero observations for messages 1438:1438 in hermes/cron_xxx!
PERFORMANCE minimal_deriver_1438_user | llm_call_duration=277403ms | observation_count=0
```
**Root cause:** qwen3 enables thinking by default. Through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, all output goes into reasoning/reasoning_content, and content comes back empty once the token budget is consumed by thinking. Honcho's json_mode=True then receives an empty string → Repair failed. This is the same failure documented in plastic-labs/honcho#716 and ollama/ollama#10976.

**Workaround (verified):** disable thinking for the deriver. Honcho's thinking_effort maps to the OpenAI reasoning_effort field, and Ollama honors reasoning_effort: "none" by turning thinking off. Set:

`DERIVER_MODEL_CONFIG__THINKING_EFFORT=none`

**Result:** llm_call_duration dropped from 277 s (failing) to ~25–90 s, and observation_count went from 0 to 5–10 per message. (I also mount a config.toml with enable_thinking = false under [deriver.model_config.overrides.provider_params.extra_body.chat_template_kwargs] plus [deriver] flush_enabled = true, but the THINKING_EFFORT=none env var alone fixed the empty-content issue.)

Thanks for the all-in-one image !!!!  
These were the only blockers after a fresh install.

title: [Bug]: macOS — managed worker reservation rejects every worker (permission_denied) after a clock correction: verify_worker_identity compares psutil create_time by exact equality
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `gateway/session_worker_reservation.py::verify_worker_identity` compares the worker's self-reported `birth` with the owner's `psutil.Process(pid).create_time()` by **exact equality**. With psutil 7.x, `create_time()` is adjusted by `_psosx.adjust_proc_create_time`, which shifts the value by `INIT_BOOT_TIME - boot_time()` — and `INIT_BOOT_TIME` is captured when psutil is imported in *that* process.

The gateway is long-lived, so its `INIT_BOOT_TIME` goes stale after a clock correction (NTP step, sleep/wake). A freshly spawned managed worker computes `birth` with a current `INIT_BOOT_TIME` (diff 0, no adjustment). Once the drift reaches ≥ 1 s, the two values differ for **every** new worker:

```
gateway.session_managed_worker: Managed worker lost: permission_denied
gateway.session_authority: Admitted turn … failed
  File "gateway/session_worker_reservation.py", line 42, in verify_worker_identity
    raise RuntimeStoreError('permission_denied')
```

Every kanban worker then exits with code 1 right after spawn, and the failure breaker blocks the cards (`gave_up`, `Kanban owner refused: Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner`). Only `hermes gateway restart` (fresh `INIT_BOOT_TIME` in the owner) clears it.

This looks like another comparison site of the same class as #118326, #123811, #128471, #135344 and #138216 (create_time drift on macOS), but this one is in the **managed-worker reservation** path, which I could not find reported. It blocks all workers at once instead of misclassifying a single one.

## Environment
- Hermes `main` @ `0ab43d4f67` (also seen on `39de69b19c`), macOS (Darwin 25.6, arm64), gateway under launchd
- psutil 7.2.2 in the gateway venv (Python 3.11.15)
- Profiles with kanban workers (default + reviewer profile); the gateway runs for hours

## Observed
4 storms in one day (07:54, 10:27, 10:55, 11:20 local time). Each lasted until the gateway was restarted, with 3–9 `permission_denied` per minute across both profiles. A single card dispatched alone also failed, so it is not concurrency-related.

## Suggested fix
Compare identity with a drift-independent value on both sides, e.g. `create_time(monotonic=True)` (psutil ≥ 7 on macOS/BSD), or allow a small tolerance (same idea as #111454 for the cron ledger). Re-reading the boot-time reference in the owner before comparing would also work.

## Workaround
An external watcher (outside the gateway, since cron jobs are not allowed to restart it — #30719) that runs `hermes gateway restart` when ≥ 4 `permission_denied` appear within 4 minutes, at most once every 15 minutes.

body:
There are 31 `FUZER_*` environment variables in `src/` today, and most of them shouldn't be environment variables:

- **Connection and secrets:** `DATABASE_URL`, `PGDATA`, `PI_WEB_API_URL`, `PI_USER`, `PI_PASSWORD`, `PI_VERIFY_TLS`, `PI_DATA_SERVER`, `PI_AF_SERVER`, `PI_AF_DATABASE`, `ADX_URL`, `ADX_TOKEN`, `ADX_DATABASE`, `ADX_CATALOG`, `ALERT_WEBHOOK`
- **Project selection:** `PACK`, `DATA_DIR`, `MAPPINGS`, `TIMESERIES`, `CACHE_DIR`, `ENV_FILE`. Most of these follow from the project name.
- **Claude:** `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_EFFORT`, `AGENT_MODEL`, `AGENT_EFFORT`, `AGENT_SPECIALIST_MODEL`, `AGENT_SPECIALIST_EFFORT`, `AGENT_FALLBACKS`
- **Operations:** `TIMEZONE`, `DAY_CLOSE_CRON`, `WORK_LEASE_SECONDS`, `WORK_MEM`

Module-level constants also hold settings that a site would want to tune. Examples are `MAX_DIAGNOSES` and `MAX_USD` in `sre_handoff.py`, `MATERIAL` in `opportunities.py`, the alarm thresholds in `alarms.py`, and `DEFAULT_MODEL` in three places (`agents`, `llm_links`, `cli`).

## Proposal
1. **One project setting.** `FUZER_PROJECT` (or `--project`) selects a project. The pack, data folder, mappings, cache and timeseries source all follow from it, with conventional paths and an optional per-project config file. Drop the variables those settings make redundant.
2. **Keep only bootstrap settings and secrets in the environment:** the database URL, and the credentials for PI, ADX and the webhook (or a secrets reference).
3. **Store everything else in the database**, in a `setting` table with `scope` (global, project or user), `key`, `value`, `updated_by` and `updated_at`. Add a typed registry in code (`settings.py`) giving each setting its name, type, default, description, valid range and whether it can be changed at runtime.
4. **A Settings page in the UI**, grouped by area (sources, Claude, SRE and handoff, reports, opportunities and alarms). It should validate input, show each setting's default, show who changed it last, and keep a history of changes.
5. **Move global constants into the registry.** Sweep the modules for tunable constants such as thresholds, caps, intervals, model ids and cron schedules. Read them through `settings.get(conn, key)`, with the constant as the default. Fixed physical and standard constants stay in code.
6. **Deprecation:** read the old variables for one release and log a warning naming the new setting.

## Done when
- `.env.example` lists at most about 6 variables.
- One place defines the default model.
- Every tunable threshold is visible and editable on the Settings page, and changes are audited.
- CI and tests run with only `FUZER_DATABASE_URL` and `FUZER_PROJECT` set.

comments.body:
## Proposed design for #131, for review before building

### 1. What stays in the environment (bootstrap and secrets only)
| Variable | Why it stays |
|---|---|
| `FUZER_DATABASE_URL` | The settings live in the database, so the URL to reach it can't be one of them. Unset: the embedded Postgres in `.fuzer/pgdata`, as today. |
| `FUZER_PROJECT` | Which project to open. Replaces `FUZER_PACK`, `FUZER_DATA_DIR`, `FUZER_MAPPINGS`, `FUZER_CACHE_DIR` and `FUZER_TIMESERIES`, which follow from the project (§2). |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | A secret. |
| `FUZER_PI_PASSWORD`, `FUZER_ADX_TOKEN`, the webhook URL | Secrets. Each source's settings name a secret by reference (`env:FUZER_PI_PASSWORD`), so a vault can supply them later. |

That's 4 core variables plus one per secret, down from 31. Everything else is a setting.

### 2. Projects
- `projects/<name>/project.yaml` holds the asset pack, data folder, mapping folders, timeseries provider, timezone and, for a fake plant, its asset and seed.
- Conventional paths apply when a value is left out: `projects/<name>/data`, `projects/<name>/mappings`, `.fuzer/cache/<name>`.
- `okan`, `offshore_demo` and `onshore_demo` ship as projects, pointing at `fakeplant/data/<asset>`.
- `fuzer --project okan …` (or `FUZER_PROJECT`) selects one. Without either, the only project present is used, or the CLI asks.
- This also ends the mismatch that tripped up the live run: `.fuzer/pgdata` holding one plant while the shell pointed at another.

### 3. The registry

## Decisions (2026-11-02)
1. **Project config: the database first, the repo as fallback.** `project` rows in the database are what's used. `projects/*.yaml` in the repo seed them, and are used when the database has no row (a fresh database, CI, the demos).
2. **Scopes: global and project.** No per-user scope for now. The registry keeps `scope` so a user scope can be added later.
3. **No replay gate.** Changing a detection threshold saves straight away; the change history records who changed it and why.

title: CI does not run the test suite on macOS or inside a Hermes session environment
body:
## Problem

The full unittest suite runs in CI on ubuntu (Python 3.11 on pull requests, plus 3.13 on pushes) and on windows (3.12): `.github/workflows/ci.yml:84-95` and `:251-263`. macOS gets only the `distribution` job, which builds and installs the package but does not run the suite (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:556-560`). Every lane starts from a clean runner environment, so no CI lane runs the suite inside a Hermes session shell.

I ran the full suite locally at 3e3f4c19e on macOS, from a shell started inside a Hermes session. Eight tests failed. None of the failures is shown to be specific to macOS or to Python 3.14. Seven of them come from the Hermes session environment leaking into the tests, which CI cannot see because CI never runs inside such a session. I am not reporting an OS bug. My question is whether CI should cover these two environments.

## Complete user goal

Contributors who run the suite on macOS, or from a Hermes or OMH TUI session (a common setup for people working on OMH), get the same result as CI.

## Intended surfaces

Not executor-specific (test suite and CI).

## Observed evidence

Environment: macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), `uv run python` reported Python 3.14.7, detached worktree at 3e3f4c19e. The shell was inside a Hermes/OMH TUI session, so `HERMES_TUI_DIR`, `HERMES_CRON_SESSION`, `HERMES_PYTHON` and other session variables were set. I planned the run with `tools/test_sharding/plan.py --shards 4` (25,648 tests discovered, 77 quarantined) and ran four shards with `tools/test_sharding/run.py --lane local --workers 2`, followed by the quarantine set.

Result: 25,483 tests executed in the shards, with 6 failures and 2 errors. The 77 quarantined tests passed.

1. Four `test_omh_resume_door` tests fail with `'HERMES_TUI_DIR' unexpectedly found in {...}`, because `HERMES_TUI_DIR` is inherited from the session: `FallbackTargetTests.test_no_node_opens_plain_hermes`, `FallbackTargetTests.test_no_termios_with_node_opens_hermes_own_tui`, `FallbackTargetTests.test_the_fallback_code_with_node_opens_hermes_own_tui` and `OmhTuiDoorTests.test_without_the_omh_tui_and_without_node_plain_hermes_runs`. #2789 fixes this leak.
2. Three more tests depend on the session environment:
   - `test_repeat_call_breaker.UnattendedLaneTest.test_cron_is_not_detectable_from_a_plugin_and_reads_as_attended` fails with `AssertionError: '' is not None` at `self.assertIsNone(os.environ.get("HERMES_CRON_SESSION"))` (`tests/test_repeat_call_breaker.py:1416`). The session exports `HERMES_CRON_SESSION=''`.
   - `test_plugin_distribution.PluginHermesAdmissionTests.test_real_admission_accepts_declared_range` (`tests/test_plugin_distribution.py:393`) fails with `observed False ... loader_probe_failed ... ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'`.
   - `test_plugin_distribution.PluginHermesAdmissionTests.test_real_admission_rejects_unsupported_version_before_register` (`tests/test_plugin_distribution.py:359-364`) errors with `CalledProcessError` from `<~/.hermes/tools/python-3.14.x>/bin/python3 -c 'from hermes_cli import __version__'`.

     Both of these tests take `HERMES_PYTHON` before anything else when they choose an interpreter: the first through `_loader_command` (`src/install/plugin_loader_observation.py:185-189`), the second through `_find_hermes_python` (`src/install/plugin_loader_observation.py:256-259`). The session set `HERMES_PYTHON` to a Hermes-managed tools `python3` that does not have `hermes_cli` installed.
3. `test_ai_job_search_state.JobStateTests.test_aggregate_proposed_state_size_preserves_bytes` (`tests/test_ai_job_search_state.py:762`) errors with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The error comes from the 15 s timeout in the `cli` helper (`tests/test_ai_job_search_state.py:112-113`), reached through the `merge(value, exit=2)` call at `:786`. I saw this with eight workers running at once (four shards × `--workers 2`), so it looks load-sensitive. I did not re-run it on its own.

Nothing above shows a macOS-specific or 3.14-spec

comments.body:
Thanks for the careful run. Here is where each of the eight results stands.

| Reported | Cause | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 `test_omh_resume_door` failures | inherited `HERMES_TUI_DIR` | fixed on `main` by your #2789 |
| `test_repeat_call_breaker...test_cron_is_not_detectable_from_a_plugin_and_reads_as_attended` | Hermes' terminal tool exports `HERMES_CRON_SESSION=''` into every shell it starts; the test asserted the variable was absent | #2814: the test now removes and sets the variable itself |
| 2 `test_plugin_distribution` real-admission tests | `HERMES_PYTHON` names an interpreter that cannot import `hermes_cli`; the gate only checked that the file exists | #2814: the gate asks the interpreter the tests would use, and skips with the reason |
| `test_ai_job_search_state...preserves_bytes` timeout | a 15 s helper timeout with eight workers running | load, as you suspected; not changed |

Reproduced here before the change, in a shell started by a Hermes session: the cron test `FAILED (failures=1)` on `main`, and the two admission tests `FAILED (failures=1, errors=1)` with `HERMES_PYTHON` pointing at an interpreter without `hermes_cli`.

One related case turned up while checking, and #2814 does not hide it: with no `HERMES_PYTHON`, when the first `hermes` on `PATH` is a small wrapper script rather than the launcher itself, the loader observation cannot trace it to a code tree and those two admission tests fail with `hermes_code_tree_absent`, on `main` as well.

This is

Decision on the two questions this issue asked: no new CI lane for now.

- **macOS and the newest Python in the test matrix:** not added. Neither your run nor ours showed a failure specific to macOS or to Python 3.14; every one of the eight results traced to the shell's environment or to load. macOS runners are slower and cost more, and the `distribution` job already builds and installs there.
- **A lane that runs with Hermes session variables set:** not added. The tests that read the session's environment are fixed at the source instead: #2789 (the four `test_omh_resume_door` tests) and #2814 (the cron test and the two real-admission tests) are both on `main`.

Two things found along the way are not fixed and are recorded here so they are not lost:

1. With no `HERMES_PYTHON`, when the first `hermes` on `PATH` is a small wrapper script rather than the launcher itself, the loader observation cannot trace it to a code tree, and the two real-admission tests fail with `hermes_code_tree_absent`. This is in the product's launcher discovery (`src/install/plugin_loader_observation.py`), not in the tests.
2. When `HERMES_PYTHON` names an interpreter that cannot import `hermes_cli`, the doctor check reports "real Hermes loader not observed (loader_probe_failed)" without naming the override or the cause.

Closing as not planned. If a failure turns up that only macOS or only a newer Python shows, please reopen with it and the matrix question gets a different answer.

title: fix(dotnet): set the .NET environment for all users and every session type, not just interactive bash
body:
## Problem
The .NET SDK is installed machine-wide at `/usr/share/dotnet`, but its environment (`DOTNET_ROOT`, `PATH`, and the `DOTNET_*` tuning variables) is only set in `/etc/bash.bashrc.d/60_dotnet.sh`. That file is sourced by **interactive bash** only. Every other kind of process on the machine sees no `dotnet` at all, including:

- non-interactive shells: `ssh host 'cmd'`, scripts, CI runners, agent tool calls
- login shells that don't source bashrc
- systemd services and user units, cron and timers
- non-bash shells, and GUI apps or IDEs started from the desktop session

Measured on a machine set up by this repo:

```
bash -lc 'command -v dotnet'   -> (nothing)
bash -ic 'command -v dotnet'   -> /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet
```

So tooling that runs non-interactively (an automation agent working over SSH, for example) concludes ".NET isn't installed" and falls back to hand-editing, for instance writing CHANGELOG.md by hand instead of using `dotnet changelog`. The only workaround is to prefix every command with `export DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/share/dotnet PATH=/usr/share/dotnet:$PATH`.

## Proposed change
Set the .NET environment globally, for all users and all process types, from one source:

1. Write the variables to a file that pam_env / systemd read for every session. That's `/etc/environment.d/60-dotnet.conf` for systemd user sessions and services, plus `/etc/environment` (or a pam_env conf) for SSH and console logins. The variables are `DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/share/dotnet`, the `DOTNET_*` settings currently exported in `60_dotnet.sh`, and `PATH` including `/usr/share/dotnet` (and `$HOME/.dotnet/tools` where the mechanism supports `$HOME`).
2. Add a `/etc/profile.d/60_dotnet.sh` so login shells get the same values.
3. Make `dotnet` resolvable without PATH as well, with a `/usr/local/bin/dotnet` symlink to `/usr/share/dotnet/dotnet`, so scripts with a minimal PATH still find it. Keep `DOTNET_ROOT` set, so apphosts and global tools resolve the runtime.
4. Keep `/etc/bash.bashrc.d/60_dotnet.sh` only for interactive-only niceties, or remove it if everything moves. The values must not be defined in two places, so generate both files from one list.

Install and uninstall it alongside install-latest-dotnet, so a machine without the SDK doesn't get a dangling PATH entry.

## Acceptance criteria
- On a freshly set-up machine, `bash -lc 'command -v dotnet'`, `bash -c 'command -v dotnet'` (via `ssh host`), `systemd-run --user --wait --pipe sh -c 'command -v dotnet; echo $DOTNET_ROOT'` and a cron job all find `/usr/share/dotnet/dotnet` with `DOTNET_ROOT` set.
- `dotnet tool restore && dotnet changelog --help` works from a non-interactive SSH command in a repo with a tool manifest.
- Each `DOTNET_*` value is defined in exactly one source file.
- Removing the SDK removes the environment entries and the symlink.

comments.body: Thanks for opening your first issue here! Please make sure you have read the contributing guidelines.

## Implementation Plan

### Files to change
- `settings/dotnet-env/dotnet.env` (new) - the single source list: `DOTNET_ROOT`, every `DOTNET_*` tuning variable, `MSBUILDTERMINALLOGGER`, `SuppressNETCoreSdkPreviewMessage`, and the PATH entry. Every other file is generated from it.
- `settings/bash.bashrc.d/60_dotnet.sh` - removed; its values move to the generated files.
- `install.d/dotnet-environment` (new) - generates and installs `/etc/environment.d/60-dotnet.conf`, `/etc/profile.d/60_dotnet.sh` and the `/usr/local/bin/dotnet` symlink from the source list, but only when `/usr/share/dotnet/dotnet` exists.
- `settings/scripts/general/install-latest-dotnet` - after the live link switch, call the environment install step so a machine gets the environment together with the SDK. It must not run the step if the install fails.
- `settings/scripts/general/uninstall-dotnet` (new) - removes the SDK, the symlink and the generated files together.
- `test/general.bats`, `test/shell-environment.bats` - tests below.
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` - document the mechanism and add the entry.

### Approach
Keep one list of variables in `settings/dotnet-env/dotnet.env` and generate from it at install time: a plain name=value file for `/etc/environment.d/60-dotnet.conf`, and a POSIX export file for `/etc/profile.d/60_dotnet.sh`, which also adds `/usr/share/dotnet` to PATH when present. A `/usr/local/bin/dotnet` symlink lets scripts with a minimal PATH find dotnet, and `DOTNET_ROOT` is still set s

## Answers to the plan's questions

Checked against an Arch install (pam 1.7.3, current systemd, OpenSSH) and this repo's `settings/bash.bashrc.d/60_dotnet.sh`.

**Q1 (literal PATH in `environment.d` / `/etc/environment`): never write a fixed literal PATH anywhere.**
- **`/etc/environment.d/60-dotnet.conf`: append, don't replace.** Assumption b is wrong for this file. environment.d(5) says the right-hand side "may reference previously defined environment variables, using the `${OTHER_KEY}` and `$OTHER_KEY` format", and its own example is `PATH=/opt/foo/bin:$PATH`. Write `PATH=$PATH:/usr/share/dotnet`, appended to match the current `_bashrc_d_path_append`, plus `DOTNET_ROOT` and the other variables. A literal PATH would replace the user manager's PATH and anything an earlier environment.d file added.
- **pam_env (SSH and console logins): no PATH line.** `/etc/environment` has no expansion, so a PATH there would have to be literal and would override every login's PATH. The `/usr/local/bin/dotnet` symlink covers this instead: sshd's built-in PATH on Arch is `/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`, so `ssh host 'command -v dotnet'` finds it.
- **`$HOME/.dotnet/tools`: only in `/etc/profile.d/60_dotnet.sh`, as assumed.**

**Q2 (whether to write `/etc/environment` for SSH): set the variables through pam_env, but in `/etc/security/pam_env.conf`, not `/etc/environment`.** `/etc/environment.d` isn't read by SSH or console sessions. The symlink only fixes PATH. profile.d isn't read b

title: Let a flag read extra, non-prefixed environment variables
body:
## Problem

A flag can fall back only to the app-prefixed environment variable. A non-secret flag gets it through a `Settings` field (`PY_IBKR_QUERY_ID`), and a secret gets `<APP>_<NAME>` (`PY_IBKR_TOKEN`). There is no way to also accept the variable name a service already uses.

Migrating `py-ibkr download` from argparse, the CLI reads `IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN` and `IBKR_FLEX_QUERY_ID`, names users already have in `.env` files, CI secrets, and cron jobs. With treaty they must either be renamed or passed on every call as `--token-from-env IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN`. `Flag` has no option for this, and reading `os.environ` in the handler trips the `env-prefix` audit rule and bypasses validation.

## Why it matters

Any CLI that wraps a third-party service inherits established variable names: `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN`. Forcing a rename is migration friction and gives agents no benefit.

There is already a precedent: login commands accept extra `token_env_vars=` beyond `<APP>_TOKEN`.

## Proposal

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Download:
    token: str = Flag(description="Flex Web Service token", env=("IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN",))
    query_id: str = Flag(description="Flex Query ID", env=("IBKR_FLEX_QUERY_ID",))
```

- `env=` lists extra variables, read after the prefixed one: `--x-from-env` / `--x-from-file` / `--x`, then `<APP>_<NAME>`, then `env` in order
- Works for secret and non-secret flags; a secret's value is still redacted everywhere
- The manifest and `--help` list the names (`secret_env_vars` for secrets, the flag description or a new key otherwise); `--show-config` reports the source as `env:IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN`
- `env-prefix` stays satisfied, since the names are declared rather than read ad hoc

## Open questions

- Should a declared `env` name be allowed to take precedence over `<APP>_<NAME>`, or always come after it?
- Should one flag be allowed several names (e.g. a deprecated alias)?

comments.body:
Triage: **postponed to 1.1**. It shares a design with #7 (see the plan there), so both ship as one `env=(...)` keyword on `Flag` and `Setting`.

Answers to the open questions, unless someone objects:

- **Precedence:** declared names always come after `<APP>_<NAME>`. The prefixed name is the one treaty documents everywhere, so it has to win; otherwise setting `PY_IBKR_TOKEN` would do nothing while a stale `IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN` is exported
- **Several names:** yes, a tuple read in order, each one optionally deprecated. That covers a service name plus an old alias

Another data point: a family of tools sharing one variable. `cloudfall` and `cloudfall-engine` both read `CLOUDFALL_PROJECT` (the project directory), documented as one name for both. On treaty the engine's prefix is `CLOUDFALL_ENGINE_`, so the shared name is outside it; the port reads it in domain code (`resolve_project_directory(args.project, os.environ, ...)`), which the `env-prefix` rule does not see because the key is read from a mapping parameter, not `os.environ.get`.

The proposed `Flag(env=("CLOUDFALL_PROJECT",))` covers it exactly:

```python
project: Path | None = Flag(default=None, description="Project directory", env=("CLOUDFALL_PROJECT",))
```

and would put the name in `--help`, the manifest, and `--show-config`, which today only the prose description does.

Triage: **implement**, for the next release candidate (moved up from 1.1). One mechanism with #7: `Flag(env=("IBKR_FLEX_TOKEN",))`, read after `<APP>_<NAME>`, a tuple in order, each name optionally deprecated. It works for secret and non-secret flags; a secret's value stays redacted, and its names join `secret_env_vars` in the manifest. The `CLOUDFALL_PROJECT` case above is covered as written. I'll link the PR here.

The implementation is in #143 (stacked on #142 for #7): the same `env=` keyword on command flags, with one precedence for argv, `--raw-payload`, `exec` and MCP. A secret's declared names join `secret_env_vars` and its value stays redacted. A plain flag's names appear in its description for now, since the spec's flag entry has no key for them (filed as cli-agent-spec/cli-agent-spec#20). A required flag with `env=` shows `required: false` on the wire, as `--x-from-env` already does. This issue closes when #143 merges.
Released in v1.0.0rc11. `uv add treaty==1.0.0rc11`

title: cron_targets walks role tasks/ files, so the cron PATH/KUBECONFIG rules check nothing
body:
## Symptom

`scripts/validate/validate_lib/cron_targets.py:iter_cron_targets` walks `ansible/roles/**/tasks/*.yml` for `ansible.builtin.cron` jobs and the shell templates they run. No role has a `tasks/` directory since H7.55, so it yields nothing. `cron_checks.py` (the PATH and KUBECONFIG rules for cron-run scripts) and `validate/shell_templates.py` therefore check an empty set. The census rows in `scripts/tests/_render_helper_rules.py` name these functions too.

Scheduled scripts now run from host-component systemd timers (`hosts/components/*/units/`), which set their own environment. The memory entry "cron inherits neither PATH nor KUBECONFIG" points at this check.

## Fix

title: bug(ckpt): OpenClaw cron uses the old install path
body:
### Component

ckpt / OpenClaw 插件

### What happened?

ws-ckpt 0.7.0 的 OpenClaw 插件仍把 `/usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt` 硬编码到 cron 命令中，但 0.7.0 起 RPM 的 `ws-ckpt-core` 将 CLI 安装到 `/usr/bin/ws-ckpt`。如果旧路径没有残留二进制或兼容链接，cron 条目可以安装成功，定时执行时却找不到命令；生成的命令还包含 `>/dev/null 2>&1`，因而错误不会显示给插件用户。

期望：插件根据其运行环境找到实际可执行的 `ws-ckpt`，并将发现的绝对路径写入 cron，使定时执行不依赖 cron 的精简 PATH；兼容 RPM、默认源码安装和自定义安装前缀。

### How can we reproduce it?

目标环境复现条件（以下完整 RPM/OpenClaw 场景尚未在本次核验中实跑）：

1. 在 Linux 上安装 ws-ckpt 0.7.0 的 core 和 plugins RPM，并确认 `/usr/bin/ws-ckpt` 可执行而 `/usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt` 不存在。
2. 在 OpenClaw 插件中配置已注册的 workspace 和 `cronSchedules: ["0 * * * *"]`，触发配置同步或 `session_start`。
3. `crontab -l` 中仍会出现：

```sh
0 * * * * /usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt checkpoint -w '/workspace' -s "cron-$(date +\%s)" -m "scheduled snapshot" --metadata '{"auto":true,"type":"cron"}' >/dev/null 2>&1
```

4. cron 到点执行的目标路径不存在；配置/同步成功不能保证定时快照执行成功。

### Diagnostic output

已核实的源码与定向回归证据：

- 官方 `ckpt/v0.7.0` 的 `src/ws-ckpt/src/plugins/openclaw/src/cron.ts` 中，`buildCronLine()` 明确使用 `/usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt`。
- 当前官方 main 基线 `5474d8af4` 仍包含同一代码。
- `src/ws-ckpt/packaging/rpm/ws-ckpt.spec.in` 安装到 `%{_bindir}/ws-ckpt`，RPM 渠道为 `/usr/bin/ws-ckpt`；默认 `make install` 仍是 `/usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt`，因此不能简单替换为另一条硬编码路径。
- 在未改运行时代码的 main 基线上，用现有 Vitest cron harness 新增 RPM PATH 断言，`CrontabManager.sync("/ws", ["0 * * * *"])` 返回 true，但生成内容与预期不符：

```text
PATH=/usr/bin
Expected: 0 * * * * '/usr/bin/ws-ckpt' checkpoint
Received: 0 * * * * /usr/local/bin/ws-ckpt checkpoint ... >/dev/null 2>&1
```

这是插件命令生成层的回归复现，`runCrontab` 使用 mock；尚不代表真实 RPM 安装、OpenClaw 宿主或 Btrfs 快照端到端验收。

### Anything else?

- Hermes 插件已使用 `shutil.which("ws-ckpt")`，此次缺陷和修复范围为 OpenClaw。
- 硬编码来自 `ec2d652fbcd1003276c22b128e8f3293b73053fc`（`fix(ckpt): use absolute path for ws-ckpt in crontab entries`）；RPM 路径变更后，该固定前缀不再适用。
- 修复须覆盖：按 PATH 顺序发现可执行文件、保存绝对路径并正确引用、CLI 不可用时不改 cron、CLI 卸载后仍能移除 cron，以及重新同步时替换旧条目而不重复或影响其他 workspace。
- 升级插件文件本身不会立即重写既有 crontab；应由后续配置同步或新会话的 cron 同步修复旧条目。
- 0.7.1 发布已暂停，待修复 PR 合并后再纳入发布基线。普通修复 PR 不修改版本元数据或 CHANGELOG。

## Symptom

The `UpsSecondaryNotReporting` annotations in `ansible/roles/k8s/observability/files/rules/other-setup-checks.yaml` (both the daniel-box and daniel-server rules, around lines 76-79 and 108-112) tell the operator to check "the `UPS secondary watchdog` cron". Point the annotations at `systemctl status homelab-ups-watchdog.timer` / `journalctl -u homelab-ups-watchdog.service` and the `/usr/lib/homelab/ups-secondary-health` path, and update the promtool test expectations to match.

title: Scheduled ticks fail silently: gh not on cron PATH
body:
## Scheduled ticks fail silently: `gh` isn't on the cron PATH

**Symptom:** from about 12:58 to 13:40, no dispatcher actions ran: Codex never reviewed #27 at `ada72a1`, #31 or #34. Yet `team tick --dry-run` from an interactive shell correctly planned "codex review #34".

**Cause:** the User Scripts reconcile script runs without `/usr/local/bin` on PATH, so `gh` fails (`{"team":{"error":"gh pr list failed: "}}`, reproduced with `env -i`). Its output goes to `/dev/null`, so every scheduled tick failed with no trace. The earlier dispatcher actions were started by hand-run ticks.

**Hot fix, applied by the homeowner on Tower:** the script now exports an explicit `PATH` and `HOME=/root`, and appends to a bounded log at `/mnt/cache/ai-supervisor/reconcile.log`. A backup of the original script was kept.

**Permanent fix (Claude; Codex reviews):**
1. `tools/install-reconcile-user-script.sh` writes the explicit PATH/HOME and the bounded log. Add a temp-root test that runs the generated script under `env -i` with a fake `gh` and `node`.
2. `team tick` reports a missing `gh` or `node` as a clear error naming the binary, and the dashboard (#32) shows "last tick failed" plus "no successful tick in more than 10 minutes".
3. Startup check: before enabling the dispatcher, the upgrade or enable procedure runs one tick under the cron environment and refuses to proceed if it fails.
4. Mark the cron path "verified working" in the handover only after a scheduled (not hand-run) tick has started a job.

comments.body:
Second failure mode, seen live at 13:50 and 13:55: `{"team":{"error":"issue or worktree already leased; stale lease requires explicit recovery"}}`. One stale lease, most likely left by the manual pause and resume of job 7829 (completed, never released), aborts the **entire** tick, so no agent gets any work.

Add to the scope:
5. A per-action failure, such as a lease conflict or a `gh` error on one PR, skips **that** action with a recorded reason, and the tick continues with the other agents and items.
6. The dispatcher releases leases for its own jobs automatically when they reach a terminal state, including jobs resumed by hand.
7. Stale leases appear on the dashboard (#32) as an attention item naming the job and the safe `release` command.
8. The hot-fixed User Scripts wrapper uses `flock` and trims the log only above a threshold. Trimming without a lock lost one tick result when two runs overlapped.

Third failure mode, seen live at 14:00. The first fully scheduled Codex review (job e6efe973, PR #36) blocked with `auth_error` 150 ms after starting. `codex` is installed at `/root/.local/bin/codex`, which is not on the cron PATH, so the preflight check `codex login status` failed. It was reported as an auth error.

Add to the scope:
9. Resolve each provider executable by an absolute path recorded at install time, or have `install-reconcile-user-script.sh` put the PATH together from the actual `command -v` results. Don't rely on the cron environment.
10. If a provider binary is missing, report it as a distinct `preflight_failed: <provider> not found`, not `auth_error`. An auth error tells the homeowner to log in again, which here would have been the wrong fix.
11. The enable procedure runs both providers' preflight checks under `env -i` with the script's PATH, and refuses to enable if either fails.

Minor: the "Needs the homeowner" notice for blocked job e6efe973 was posted on PR #36 three times (14:05, 14:10, 14:15), once per tick. Notify once per job and state, and add a follow-up only if the state changes.

Also: intermittent `gh issue list failed: error connecting to api.github.com` (13:43 and the 14:35 scheduled tick), with success on the ticks either side. Retry transient GitHub transport errors within the tick (bounded, for example 3 tries with backoff) before failing it, and show a count of consecutive failed ticks on the dashboard (#32) rather than one failure.

Also: the dispatcher-recorded verdict for job 45754a21 (PR #36, CHANGES at 5b1a729) was posted twice, at 15:15 and 15:20. Post each verdict exactly once, keyed on job + head, and make posting idempotent across ticks. The same notify-once rule as for "needs the homeowner".

**Overseer: two missing dispatcher rules (observed 15:30–16:07; the loop stalled with nothing running).**

12. **Red CI on your own PR → fix job.** PR #38 (this issue) has failing `project-contract` and `test` at a140a4f. The review rule needs green CI, and no rule sends a red PR back to its author, so the PR sits there forever. Add: if an agent's own open, non-draft PR has a completed failing check on its head, give the author a fix job (bounded by `max_fix_attempts`), with the failing check names in the prompt.
13. **Merge conflict on your own PR → rebase job.** #36 and #27 are `dirty` (conflicting with main). GitHub won't run `pull_request` CI on a conflicting PR, so #36 can never go green. Add: if an agent's own PR conflicts with main, give the author a **conflict-only rebase** job. Its post-condition is a new head that is mergeable, plus a range-diff comment. A previously recorded PASS for the old head only carries over when the range-diff shows conflict resolution only, and the opposite agent still re-checks it (the same rule as the manual #21/#31 re-checks).

Priority order per agent: rebase > CI fix > review fix > review > implement.

**Overseer decision (2026-10-30): split #38.** The enable gate (item 11, plus the gate parts of item 3) moves to #40. #38 keeps items 1–2 and 4–10, 12 and 13: PATH and HOME, explicit binaries, per-action skip, automatic lease release, notify-once and verdict-once, GitHub retries, and the rebase and red-CI rules.

Also a bug: `max_fix_attempts` (2) did not stop #38 after two rounds. It reached five CHANGES verdicts without a needs-homeowner hand-off. Fix it in #38: count fix attempts per PR, not per head, and after the limit post one needs-homeowner notice and stop dispatching fixes for that PR.

PR #38 merged at `351cff2ff57f4ddd8a6931d9b7bd173c6b56103a` by the dispatcher. Gates: PASS from `codex` (job `9f58f6f5d44586fe4fd7a264a9d0b49b`) recorded for this exact head, all checks green, mergeable. Merged is not deployed or verified working.

title: [75.29] infra — pin container base images by digest, run the backup container as non-root, add healthchecks
body:
## Goal

Every container image in `Dockerfile`, `scripts/backup/Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` is pinned as `name:tag@sha256:<multi-arch index digest>`; Dependabot bumps them (coverage added by #2334). The backup container runs as a non-root user and no longer writes S3/DB secrets into a crontab file. `app` and `nginx` have healthchecks, and nginx starts only after `app` is healthy.

Verified today:
- Floating: `Dockerfile:4` `node:26-alpine`; `docker-compose.yml:55` `redis:7-alpine`, `:77` `postgres:16-alpine`, `:162,175` `certbot/certbot` (no tag), `:184` `nginx:1.27-alpine`; `scripts/backup/Dockerfile:6` `alpine:3.21`. `chrislusf/seaweedfs:4.47` (`:102`) has a tag but no digest.
- Backup: `scripts/backup/Dockerfile` has no `USER`. `entrypoint.sh` writes every secret (`DATABASE_URL`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, …) into `/etc/crontabs/root` because busybox `crond` does not pass the container env to jobs, and busybox `crond` needs root to switch users. **Correction to the finding:** the container holds the age *public* key only (`BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `docker-compose.yml:140`), not the private key. Fix: `supercronic` (Alpine 3.21 community package `supercronic-0.2.33-r5`, checked with `apk search`). It runs as any user and passes its own environment to jobs, so the crontab holds only the schedule.
- No healthcheck on `app` or `nginx`; `nginx.depends_on.app` is `service_started` (`:196-198`).
- `yarn@1.22.22` (`Dockerfile:12`) is installed by exact version. npm checks the registry's `sha512` integrity on install, so **no change**.
- Redis `requirepass`: **skipped**. Redis binds `127.0.0.1` + the internal network (`:68-69`), and a password would ripple into `REDIS_URL` for the app, `scripts/test-env.sh` slots and every test run. YAGNI until Redis leaves the host.
- `scripts/check-node-version.mjs:67` reads `FROM node:(\d+)-`, which still matches `node:26-alpine@sha256:…`.

## Files

- `Dockerfile` — digest-pin `node:26-alpine`
- `docker-compose.yml` — digest-pin 6 images; `app` + `nginx` healthchecks; `nginx` waits for healthy `app`
- `scripts/backup/Dockerfile` — digest-pin `alpine:3.21`; add `supercronic`; non-root `USER`; `ENV TZ=Asia/Dhaka`
- `scripts/backup/entrypoint.sh` — write a schedule-only crontab to a user-writable path; `exec supercronic`
- `scripts/backup/README.md` — "runs as non-root via supercronic; logs go to `docker compose logs backup`"
- `.env.example` — `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` comment (line 168): "crond syntax" → "standard 5-field cron (supercronic)"
- `scripts/check-node-version.spec.mjs` — one case: digest-pinned `FROM` still parses
- `docker/test/compose.infra.test.sh` (new) — picked up by the `infra` CI job from #2312

## Steps

2. **Resolve digests**: for each image, `docker buildx imagetools inspect <name:tag> --format '{{json .Manifest.Digest}}'`. title: Follow-up: trap wrapper strings, crontab -u<user>, and remaining interpreter names after #748
body:
Follow-up from the code review of the #748 PR (approved with no critical/high findings).

## Medium (Allow on a dangerous shape)
- **trap action hides wrapper shell strings**: `trap_action_runs_interpreter` calls `command_line_stdin_sinks_with(.., direct_only = true)`, so `curl x | trap 'flock l -c sh' EXIT` and `curl x | trap 'strace -o "|sh" true' EXIT` are Allow while the un-trapped forms Block. Fix: pass `direct_only = false` (the action string shrinks per nesting and `wrapper_shell_string_sinks` has its own depth cap), or run `wrapper_shell_string_sinks` over the scan's commands.
- **crontab glued `-u<user>`**: `crontab_reads_stdin` reads `-uroot` / `-ualice` as containing `-l`/`-r`/`-e`, so `curl x | crontab -uroot` is Allow (installs the piped crontab). Treat `-u<value>` / `--user=<value>` as a consumed value before the letter check.

## Low
- Over-asks: `curl x | crontab --help`, `-V`, `-n`; `n=5; m=$n; [[ $m -gt 0 ]]` (env.exact does not chain).
- `n=$(curl x); let "n > 0"` and `declare -i m=$n` are Allow (arithmetic floor covers `[[ ]]` only; pre-existing).
- Remote/container and stdin-tool names still Allow: `sshpass -p x ssh host`, `lxc exec`, `incus exec`, `multipass exec`, `vagrant ssh -c sh`, `mosh`, `rsh`, `plink`, `autossh`, `oc rsh`, `kubectl attach -i`, `docker attach`, `nvim -`, `gvim -`, `view -`, `mariadb`, `mongosh`, `octave`, `gnuplot`, `emacs --script /dev/stdin`, and a bare `curl x | fakeroot` (wrapper with no command runs a shell).

title: BUG: backup scripts silently broken (paths, container names, pruning)
body:
BUG: backup scripts have been silently broken for months

**Evidence (2026-09-28)**
- Crontab runs `~/projects/docker/immich-daily-backup.sh` and `backup-databases.sh`, but both scripts were moved to `scripts/backup/`. `~/backups/immich-daily/cron.log` is full of `not found`. The last Immich-daily backup is `20260119`, and the last files in `/mnt/boston/docker-backups` were from `20260306`.
- Both scripts use container `immich_postgres` with user `postgres`. The container is now `immich-db` and its user is `immich` (`docker inspect immich-db`).
- `backup-databases.sh` pipes `docker exec … | gzip`, so a failed dump still prints "✓ Immich backup successful" and leaves a 20-byte `.sql.gz`.
- The retention `find … -mtime +30 -delete` runs whether or not the new backup worked. The first run after months of downtime deleted every older backup, including the last Outline dump. Outline has since been removed.
- The script still references Outline, and Trilium is referenced but should be checked.
- Immich already writes its own nightly dumps (`/mnt/boston/media/pictures/immich-storage/backups/immich-db-backup-*.sql.gz`, about 685 MB, current through 2026-09-28).

**Proposed fix**
- Remove the Immich step from `backup-databases.sh` and retire `immich-daily-backup.sh`, relying on Immich's built-in backups. Otherwise, fix the container name and user.
- Add `set -o pipefail` and treat a dump that is empty or tiny as a failure.
- Only prune after a successful backup, and always keep the newest N files regardless of their age.
- Fix the crontab paths, or remove those lines once Dagu `server-backups` is green.

comments.body:
Brandon chose to drop the Immich step. Implemented; uncommitted, In Review.

- `backup-databases.sh`: Immich removed. `pipefail` added. A dump smaller than 1 KB counts as failed. Each service prunes only after its own backup succeeds, and the newest 7 are always kept. The script exits 1 if anything fails. RomM credentials now come from the container env instead of being hardcoded. Trilium is backed up with `sqlite3 .backup` into a local temp file, because the database is in WAL mode and SQLite can't lock files on the SMB mount.
- `server-backups.yaml`: Immich step removed.
- `immich-daily-backup.sh` and `setup-automated-backups.sh` deleted (`git rm`).

Verification: `dagu start server-backups` → `Result: Succeeded`. RomM is 3.4 MB and ends with `-- Dump completed`. Jellyfin is 68 MB. The Trilium gz is 1.6 MB, passes `integrity_check`, and has 648 notes. GreatReads is OK. An earlier run failed on Trilium with `database is locked`, and the check correctly marked the step red.

Still for Brandon: remove the two stale crontab lines (`backup-databases.sh`, `immich-daily-backup.sh`).
Done in 4b48c1e (v1.3.17).

title: sec/host-4: srv1/srv2 host + Incus container hardening review (privesc, escape, persistence)
body:
Parent epic: #1717

## Goal

Assume the edge is eventually lost: what does the attacker get from `srv1`/`srv2` hosts and the Incus containers, and how fast does it become root on the host?

## 1. SSH and host access
- `sshd_config`: `PermitRootLogin`, `PasswordAuthentication`, `AllowUsers`, port, `MaxAuthTries`; is root password auth enabled (the `~/.prod` `SRV1_PASS`/`SRV2_PASS` pattern suggests yes → P1)?
- `fail2ban` present and covering sshd?
- authorized keys inventory: unknown key present = P0.
- host firewall default policy (`iptables -L`, `netfilter-persistent` rules drift vs. what INFRA.md documents).

## 2. Incus configuration review (container → host)
```bash
for c in $(incus list --format csv -c n); do
  echo "== $c"; incus config show $c | grep -Ei 'security\.privileged|security\.nesting|raw\.lxc|limits\.|devices:'; 
  incus config device show $c
done
```
Red flags: `security.privileged=true`, host path mounted into a container (`source=/opt/gbo` or `/`), `raw.lxc` with `lxc.cap.keep=all`, `lxc.mount.entry=/` — any of these turns a botserver RCE into host root.
Also: `incus config show --expanded`, unix socket permissions (`/var/lib/incus/unix.socket` group), `incus` in sudoers for `gbuser` (the CI runner!) — a compromised runner can `incus exec` **any** container as root. That is the intended CI design today; document it and confirm the runner cannot be reached from a container.

## 3. Inside the `bot` container
- Process users: botserver running as root? `ps -o user,pid,cmd -C botserver`.
- `/opt/gbo/bin` permissions and ownership (the guide says `gbuser:gbuser` — verify on both hosts).
- setuid/setgid inventory: `find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null`.
- writable paths that botserver reads: `/opt/gbo/conf`, `/opt/gbo/work`, bot drive mounts — can an uploaded file land somewhere executable (`/opt/gbo/bin`, `PATH` dirs, `systemd` unit dirs)?
- systemd units: unexpected units/timers, `ExecStart` pointing at writable paths, `Restart=always` loops that could mask tampering.
- cron (`/etc/cron*`, `crontab -l` per user) and `at`.
- Capabilities: `getcap -r / 2>/dev/null`.
- Docker socket / Incus socket inside containers: absent?
- Kernel keyring / `core_pattern`.

## 4. Persistence and lateral movement paths
- Container-to-container: can `bot` reach `tables:5432`, `vault:8200`, `cache:6379`, `drive:9000` with credentials it should not have? Enumerate what `.env`/Vault path a container can read and which other services that unlocks.
- `email` now lives on srv1 with an encrypted credential set — check DNAT/SNAT symmetry so mail cannot be used as a spoofing relay (see INFRA.md mail migration).
- Backup scripts (`backup-local-host.sh`, `backup-remote.sh`) — do they write world-readable archives containing `/opt/gbo/data/vault`?
- `~/.prod` on the admin workstation: mode, and whether it is inside any synced/git directory.

## 5. Disk / availability (non-destructive)
- `df -h /`, swap usage, log growth, `incus` storage pool usage — the host already hit 100% once and killed PostgreSQL (INFRA.md). Confirm the `gbo-postgres.service` guard is active on both hosts.
- Any unbounded log path an unauthenticated request can inflate (WS connect spam → `botserver.log`)?

## 6. Supply chain from the host
- `forgejo-runner` runs in host mode with limited sudo (`incus`). Review: which repos can it build, where do secrets come from, can a PR from a non-admin branch trigger a deploy? (`alm-release.yml` downloads a GH release, verifies sha256, deploys — verify the verify step is fail-closed.)
- Is `sccache`/`~/.cargo` shared in a way a build script (`build.rs`) can poison for another project?

## Deliverable

`/tmp/opencode/pentest/host/hardening.md`:

| Area | Finding | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|

And one issue per finding. Prioritize anything that converts *any* app-level RCE into host root.

## Done when

- [ ] Both hosts have an Incus config snapshot in evidence.
- [ ] No container is privileged / has a host path mount (or it i

comments.body:
## Blocked on #1718 + host access — no host reviewed

No SSH, Incus, systemd, sudo, cron or filesystem review has been executed. Every item in this issue needs `srv1`/`srv2` read-only access and the RoE sign-off.

The checklist is ready: `sshd_config` (root/password auth, `AllowUsers`, `MaxAuthTries`, fail2ban, authorized keys), `incus config show` per container (`security.privileged`, host-path mounts, `raw.lxc`), `gbuser → sudo incus` blast radius, botserver process user and `/opt/gbo/bin` ownership, setuid/setgid/capabilities, writable paths botserver reads, systemd timers, cron/at, container-to-container credential reach (`.env` → Vault/DB/MinIO), backup archive permissions, disk growth, and the `forgejo-runner` deploy path (fail-closed sha256 check).

The deliverable will be `/tmp/opencode/pentest/host/hardening.md` with a finding/severity/fix table and one issue per root-path conversion. Incus config snapshots are captured before any change.

Note: the offline desktop payload audit found and fixed two corrupt installer caches (#1724); that is the only host-adjacent work done so far, and it was local to this workstation.

## Host/Incus hardening complete — matrix in `/tmp/opencode/pentest/host/hardening.md`

Both hosts audited with the owner's authorization. No Incus snapshots were
created (owner instruction); every config was copied to `/tmp` before editing.

### Fixed

| Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---------|-----|----------|
| Vault sealed; botserver crash-loop (`NRestarts=10532`), `/api/health` 502 | Unsealed 3-of-5 keys | `sealed=false`, botserver `/health` 200, public `/api/health` 200 |
| Unseal keys mode 0644 | `chmod 600` | `600 root:root` |
| srv1 public 5432/8443/5858/5859 | Removed INPUT rules | all blocked; SSH/443 work |
| All containers reach the Incus socket proxy (8591) | Restrict to `bot` | bot 200, others blocked |
| All containers reach Chromium CDP proxy (9223) | Restrict to `desktop1` | desktop1 200, others blocked |
| Postgres `pg_hba` `0.0.0.0/0 trust` | Narrowed to 10/8 + Incus IPv6 /64 | reloaded, health 200 |
| Valkey no password | `requirepass` + botserver cache URL | `NOAUTH` / `PONG`, health 200 |
| srv2 INPUT policy ACCEPT exposing 6080/5901/8443 | DROP policy + explicit allows | SSH works, those three blocked |

### Residual risks (documented, not fixed)

- botserver/botui/node run as root and the bot container reaches the full Incus API (Vibe requirement); the proxy is restricted to that container.
- Qdrant has no API key because the in-tree client has no key support; not externally exposed.
- Postgres still uses `trust` inside 10/8; scram needs every service p

## Post-fix drift detected and corrected (srv2 VNC ports)

During the final re-test at 22:36 UTC the srv2 INPUT chain showed **ACCEPT
rules for 6080 and 5901 back above the DROPs**, with large packet counters —
VNC/noVNC was reachable from the internet again even though the earlier check
had shown it blocked.

Cause: the `desktop2.pragmatismo.com.br` Caddy vhost proxies to the **srv2
public IP on 6080**, so the blanket DROP broke the vhost and the blanket
ACCEPT rules had been (re)added. No cron/systemd/iptables script that adds
them was found; treat it as manual drift and re-check after any host change.

Corrected with a source-restricted rule instead of a blanket open:

```text
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 6080 -s <srv1 egress IP> -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 6080 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 5901 -j DROP
```

Verification:

- `https://desktop2.pragmatismo.com.br/` → **302** to `/vnc_auto.html`
  (the Caddy path still works).
- check-host.net, 3 independent external nodes:
  - port 22 → open 3/3 (control)
  - port 6080 → blocked 3/3
  - port 5901 → blocked 3/3
  - port 8443 → blocked 3/3
- `chat.pragmatismo.com.br`: 443 open 3/3; 5432/8443/5858/5859 blocked
  3/3 (5858 on 2 nodes).

No other sensitive public ACCEPT exists on srv1: the only entries above the
policy are the container-to-host DROPs for 8591/9223 and the Incus-generated
bridge rules; there is no public ACCEPT for 5432/6379/8200/6333/6334/9100/
4747/5858/5859/8443.

title: [Bug]: Docker already has an entry in Crontab
body:
### User story

I want the crontab entry to be removed so users are able to set their own wihtout having to remove/comment it out every time the container is restarted.

### Game

PaperMC

### Linux distro

Ubuntu 22.04

### Command

command: update

### Further information

There is a cron entry in the container by default:
```bash
*/60 * * * * /app/pmcserver update > /dev/null 2>&1
```
I don't know if this is intentional, but it is very annoying because I'd like to set my own update interval without having to modify the actual application code. I didn't think it was necessary to make an issue for such a small problem. Thanks!

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the container lol

comments.body: Which image are you using? I couldn't find any cron entries on the [latest GHCR build](https://github.com/gameservermanagers/docker-gameserver/pkgs/container/gameserver/334884938?tag=pmc).

Maybe it's because I'm using the Docker Hub image?:
```yaml
services:
  linuxgsm-pmc-bind:
    image: gameservermanagers/gameserver:pmc
    # image: ghcr.io/gameservermanagers/gameserver:pmc
```
Here's a [video ](https://streamable.com/yk75bo )showing the latest image.

Never mind, [you're right!](https://github.com/GameServerManagers/docker-linuxgsm/blob/082dd9c187efbcb3a4cae754557f7f7088a16c2b/entrypoint-user.sh#L94-L98) I was entering the container without specifying the `linuxgsm` user.

I agree that having only the docker images preconfigured to update every hour is pretty weird.

[I've made a PR for this](https://github.com/GameServerManagers/docker-linuxgsm/pull/70), hopefully it gets merged!

I was certain there are other crontab -related issues already, and there are. At least https://github.com/GameServerManagers/LinuxGSM/issues/4584 and https://github.com/GameServerManagers/LinuxGSM/pull/4508 . IIRC I've seen some discussion in another  issue somewhere but can not find it ATM (**EDIT:** realized the latter has nothing to do with the docker images per se). I'm mentioning these here so that everyone is up to date on the feature / issues and pull requests, so that perhaps a common fix can be found.
 
I agree the default crontab entry needs to go. It is intrusive, as it interrupts gameplay on servers which do not need to be on the bleeding edge and get frequent updates. The users should decide. Currently, I run 'crontab -r' after each reboot and update of the image, but I feel I should not need to.
any updates on this?? I don't want my server suddenly start autoupdate at the pick online!

I've realized one can set `UPDATE_CHECK=0`. This is not documented (AFAIK), but will skip creating the crontab on every restart of the container (or set it to some other value if want something else than hourly checks).

I've brewed an implementation for a persistent crontab within the container.

The Docker image README now documents the update settings (GameServerManagers/docker-gameserver#155, thanks @WildPenquin):

- `UPDATE_CHECK` sets the scheduled update interval (1 to 59 minutes). `UPDATE_CHECK=0` turns the scheduled check off, so the container stops writing its own crontab entry on start.
- `UPDATE_ON_START=false` skips the update when the container starts.

That covers setting your own interval or turning the default entry off. A custom crontab still lives inside the container, so it is lost when the container is recreated. Persistent custom crontabs are tracked in #4584 (and GameServerManagers/docker-linuxgsm#94 / #95).
