title: cron remove and learn remove exit 0 when nothing matches
body:
### Existing issues
I searched open issues for "Job not found" / "cron remove" exit code and found none.

### KiroCrew version
0.12.0 (main at c103936381)

### Platform
Linux

### What happened
`kirocrew cron remove <unknown id>` prints `Job not found: <id>` and exits **0**. `kirocrew learn remove <query>` with no match prints `No lessons match: <query>` and exits **0**. A script that chains with `&&` reads the failure as success.

The sibling verbs already fail: `cron pause` / `cron resume` with an unknown id exit **1**, and `docs/system-specs/modules/cli.md` (the `cron pause/resume/trigger` row) documents that.

Code:
- `src/kiro_crew/cli_commands_cron.py` lines 739-743: the `remove` branch prints `Job not found` and returns.
- `src/kiro_crew/cli_commands_cron.py` lines 745-757: `pause` / `resume` call `sys.exit(1)` on the same miss.
- `src/kiro_crew/cli_commands_learn.py` line 300: the `remove` branch prints `No lessons match` and returns.

### Steps to reproduce
Run with a throwaway home:
```
export HOME=$(mktemp -d) KIROCREW_HOME=$HOME/.kiro/crew
kirocrew cron remove nosuchid;  echo $?   # Job not found: nosuchid   -> 0
kirocrew cron pause nosuchid;   echo $?   # Job not found: nosuchid   -> 1
kirocrew learn remove nosuchrule; echo $? # No lessons match: nosuchrule -> 0
```

### Expected
A miss exits 1 and writes its message to stderr, so `&&` chains stop.

### Anything else
`cron update` with an unknown id has the same shape, but its block is being edited by open PR #24943, so it is a follow-up after #24943 lands, not part of this fix. The `--managed-by` path of `cron remove` (`No job is managed by: <x>`) is a bulk "remove all of mine" and stays exit 0: an empty set is not a failure there.

title: Deploy check: an event the site's cron ran meanwhile counts as a failed cron run
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh` reported a network deploy of 1.3.175 as failed on one site while the plugin updated and loaded fine everywhere:

```
site https://<site>/	status=active-network	purged=yes	cron=4/5	home=200 pinned	FAIL: cron seoprostack_keep_settings failed (exit 1: Error: Invalid cron event 'seoprostack_keep_settings' )
```

`run_site_cron()` (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` L635–674) lists the plugin's scheduled events first (`cron_list_code`), then runs each with `wp cron event run <hook>`. `seoprostack_keep_settings` is a single event scheduled after an update (`SEOProStack_Presets_Keep`, `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-keep.php` L112–113). On a host whose own cron job runs WP-Cron every minute, the event can run (and so leave the list) between the deploy's listing and its run. WP-CLI then exits 1 with `Invalid cron event`, and the check counts a failure that is not one: the callback did run, in the site's own cron.

Not the same race as #1362 (inside Keep pages cached).

## Fix

In `run_site_cron()`, when the run exits non-zero and its output is WP-CLI's `Invalid cron event '<hook>'` with no fatal error or database error in it, count the event as run by the site's cron: a note (`cron <hook> ran meanwhile`) in `CRON_WARN`, not `CRON_FAILURE`, and not in `CRON_HOOKS_RUN` (it did not run in the deploy's process). Every other non-zero exit stays a failure.

Deploy tooling only: no changelog entry (`STANDARDS.md` docs rule).

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh` clean.
- Read-only: on the affected network, `wp cron event list --fields=hook,next_run_relative | grep seoprostack_keep_settings` shows the event gone or rescheduled, consistent with the site's cron having run it.
- Next fleet deploy: no `Invalid cron event` FAIL lines; any race shows as a note.

title: A dead cron scheduler is silent, and the repair loses login auto-start
body:
## Why

Day Desk's cron scheduler stopped firing without saying so, and the only repair that worked was a gateway restart that also **lost login auto-start**. From this machine on 11 Nov:

```
$ hermes -p day-desk cron list          # factory-drive, every 5m
    Overdue: 19:20:56 (29m ago — the job has not fired; is the scheduler running?)

$ hermes -p day-desk gateway restart
⚠ launchd cannot manage the gateway on this macOS version (launchctl exit 5)
✓ Started gateway as a background process instead
  It will NOT auto-start at login or auto-restart on crash.
```

So the factory's only autonomous wake path can die silently and stay dead, and the fix leaves it unable to come back after a reboot. A factory that needs a person to notice "the job has not fired" is not the architecture (ADR-0130, ADR-0135).

## Acceptance

- A job that has not fired when it is due is visible where the factory is read — done when: `factory_status` reports the driving job's last fire and whether the scheduler is alive, and a test covers a stale and a live scheduler.
- The RUNBOOK's install step is the one that survives a reboot on this macOS — done when: the step that starts the gateway at login is documented with the exit code it fails with today, and a test asserts the runbook names it.
- Losing the scheduler is an event, not a silence — done when: the factory-watch path reports a scheduler that has been overdue for two intervals, once.

## Paths

- `factory_mcp/tools.py` — `factory_status`'s runtime section
- `tenant/hermes/config.yaml`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`
- `tests/test_mcp_server.py`, `tests/test_hermes.py`

## Evidence

The two command outputs above, 11 Nov 19:45 and 19:52 IST.

All three are code, docs and tests in this repo. Nothing will restart or re-register the gateway/scheduler as part of the pass.

title: core: a failed brain maintain cron run's error message does not name the failing step
body:
## Context

Split on 2026-11-02 from #3357.

When `brain maintain` fails under cron, the run's `cron_runs.error_message` gives only the exit code and the last stderr. On a hosted install whose `maintain` failed its `git` step every day, the record read `exit code 2` followed by unrelated provider log lines. The failing step was visible only in the job's stdout report.

From source at `3984040f1`:

- `brain maintain` collects one `{ step, result }` entry per step and prints the report to stdout (text or `--json`). It returns exit code 2 when any result starts with `FAILED` (`packages/core/src/cli/commands/maintain.ts:191-199`). It writes nothing to stderr about which steps failed.
- The cron wrapper records `exit code N; stderr tail: …` from the last 2,000 characters of stderr (`STDERR_TAIL_CHARS`, `packages/ui-server/src/cron/run-job.ts:21`; message at lines 335-337). Steps such as embedding write many stderr lines (`SKIP embed batch: …`), so the tail holds those lines and nothing about the failed step.

## Scope

- When `brain maintain` exits non-zero, its **last** stderr line names every failed step and the start of its result, for example `brain maintain: FAILED step(s): git (fatal: sha1 file … Out of diskspace)`. This holds in both text and `--json` modes. Bound the line so it fits well inside the cron tail.
- Nothing else changes: stdout, the `--json` shape and exit codes stay as they are.

## Out of scope

- Parsing job stdout in the cron wrapper, or a structured failure field in `cron_runs`.
- Notifications for repeated cron failures.
- The git space limit itself (#3357) and the Gemini key failure (#3363).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A core test runs `brain maintain` with one step forced to fail (for example a git failure fixture as in `packages/core/tests/maintain.test.ts`). It asserts that the last stderr line names that step and that stdout and `--json` are byte-identical to before. It fails on current main.
- [ ] A cron test runs a job whose command writes more than `STDERR_TAIL_CHARS` of unrelated stderr and then exits through `brain maintain`'s failure path. It asserts that `cron_runs.error_message` contains the failed step's name.
- [ ] A successful `brain maintain` writes no such line.

## Verification

`bun run test packages/core/tests/maintain.test.ts packages/ui-server/tests/cron-run-job.test.ts`, with the failing-first receipt.

## Contract impact

None. `brain maintain --json`'s shape and exit codes are unchanged. Stderr text is not contract.

title: Proper database backups
body:
Today `scripts/backup.sh` runs from the host's cron: a nightly `sqlite3 .backup` into `backups/` on the same box, kept 14 days. Getting copies off the box is left to the host, so a lost disk or host takes the backups with it.

Figure out:
- [x] Off-box destination (Proxmox Backup Server, rclone to object storage, …) and who owns the credentials
- [x] Retention (daily/weekly/monthly?) and encryption at rest
- [x] Restore drill: restore a backup into the dev server and check it serves and accepts a login
- [x] Alerting when a backup fails or goes stale (cron runs silently today)
- [x] Whether the backup belongs in compose (sidecar) instead of host cron
- [x] README Deploy section updated with the result

comments.body:
## Decision: rclone → Cloudflare R2, encrypted

Tried on dev (2026-10-23): upload and `cryptcheck` work. Restore drill postponed so testers aren't disturbed.

- **Destination:** Cloudflare R2, one bucket per environment (`poroleague-backups`, `poroleague-dev-backups`). R2 tokens scope to a bucket, not a prefix, so a shared bucket would let a compromised dev box delete prod backups.
- **Encryption:** `rclone crypt` on top of R2. The DB holds Discord user ids and live access tokens: fine plain on the box, not in a bucket.
- **Retention:** local 14 days (`backup.sh`), remote via an R2 lifecycle rule (prod 30 days, dev 7).
- **Upload with `rclone copy`, never `sync`:** `sync` would mirror a wiped or tampered local `backups/` and delete the remote copies.
- **Credentials:** R2 keys and crypt passwords live in `/root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf` (root, `chmod 600`) and in the password manager (one entry per environment). **Not in `.env`:** compose passes it into the app container, and the app never needs R2.
- **Host cron, not a compose sidecar:** keeps the bucket credentials out of the app's containers.

## Prod setup

On the prod host, as **root** (the backup cron runs as root).

### 1. Cloudflare

1. **R2 → Create bucket** `poroleague-backups`.
2. Bucket **Settings → Object lifecycle rules**: delete objects 30 days after upload.
3. **R2 → Manage API tokens → Create API token**: **Object Read & Write**, scoped to `poroleague-backups` only. Save the access key id, secret and endpoi

## Done

- PR #85: `backup.sh` uploads with `rclone copy --max-age 3d` to `r2crypt` and pings healthchecks.io last. It fails when the DB is missing, backups are root-only, and the README has a Backups section. `--max-age` keeps `copy` from re-uploading what the lifecycle rule deleted (dev keeps 14 days locally, 7 in R2).
- Dev: remotes renamed to `r2`/`r2crypt`, lifecycle rule now 7 days, crontab `30 4 * * *`, restore drill from R2 passed (integrity ok, counts match, login writes).
- Prod: bucket `poroleague-backups` (30 days), bucket-scoped token (403 on the dev bucket), remotes, ping file, crontab `0 4 * * *`. The first real backup comes after the first deploy (#86); until then the nightly run fails with `no database` and alerts.

title: fix(docker): run backup image as non-root with health probe
body:
The backup image runs its most sensitive job as root with no supervision.

File infrastructure/backup/Dockerfile builds an alpine image that installs database clients and the AWS CLI, copies the backup script, and runs cron as PID 1, all as uid 0 with no USER instruction and no HEALTHCHECK. The cron job ships database dumps to object storage using cloud credentials present in the container, so a breakout here trades directly on backup contents and cloud keys. A dead cron daemon looks identical to a healthy one to the orchestrator.

What I would change:
Create an unprivileged backup user, give it ownership of the log file and data paths it needs, run the container as that user, and add a HEALTHCHECK that fails when the cron process disappears. The schedule, the backup script and the installed toolset stay exactly the same.

`dev-ops/factory/tick.sh` runs as a plain cron job (`0 * * * * ...`, see `dev-ops/factory/README.md:25,67`) and currently has minimal observability: it logs human-readable lines to stdout via `log()` and errors to stderr via `die()` (`tick.sh:45-46`). 2. Make cron output deterministic, e.g. `0 * * * * /path/to/repo/dev-ops/factory/tick.sh >> /var/log/factory/tick.jsonl 2>&1` (or a small wrapper).
3. Run an **OpenTelemetry Collector**

title: Add Telegram notifications for S3 backup destinations
body:
### What problem will this feature address?

Currently, Dokploy supports backup storage destinations such as S3, but there is no easy way to integrate Telegram for backup monitoring and notifications. This makes it harder to know when a backup succeeds or fails, especially for self-hosted environments that rely on Telegram as a primary alert channel.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add Telegram support for backup workflows related to S3 destinations. I would like Dokploy to be able to notify a Telegram chat/channel about backup status, including success, failure, and maybe relevant logs when a backup is uploaded to S3. If possible, this could also be configured as part of the backup destination setup so users can monitor and react to backup events directly in Telegram.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

We can already monitor backups through the dashboard or external scripts, but there is no native Telegram integration for backup alerts. Alternative solutions include custom cron jobs, external scripts, or using other notification channels, but native support would be much easier to maintain and more reliable for users relying on Telegram.

### Additional context

This would be especially useful for self-hosted deployments and teams that use Telegram for operational alerts. It would help ensure backup failures are noticed quickly without checking the dashboard or the S3 bucket manually.

### Will you send a PR to implement it?

No

comments.body: DOK-915

Hello, this is already supported!

Go to **Settings → Notifications**, add a **Telegram** notification, and turn on **Database Backup**, **Volume Backup** and/or **Dokploy Backup**. You'll get a message when a backup succeeds or fails, including the error message on failure.

Closing this, but feel free to reopen if something's missing.

title: [0.1.8, Windows] Every `openminion cron create --cron ...` fails with `unknown timezone: UTC` (missing `tzdata` dependency)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, any recurring cron schedule is rejected, including the default timezone:

```
"error": "Invalid schedule: unknown timezone: UTC"
```

Windows ships no IANA time zone database, so Python's `zoneinfo` needs the `tzdata` package. `openminion` does not declare it. One-shot `--at` jobs work because they do not resolve a zone.

## Environment

- openminion 0.1.8 (PyPI) and `dev` at `b642697`, fresh `uv venv -p 3.12` + `uv pip install openminion==0.1.8`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.22631, Python 3.12.11
- `python -c "import tzdata"` gives `ModuleNotFoundError`

## Steps to reproduce

```powershell
uv venv -p 3.12 .venv; uv pip install --python .venv\Scripts\python.exe openminion==0.1.8
& .venv\Scripts\openminion.exe --home-root .\proj --data-root .\proj\.openminion config init --provider echo
& .venv\Scripts\openminion.exe --home-root .\proj --data-root .\proj\.openminion cron create --instruction "say hi" --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" --json
& .venv\Scripts\openminion.exe --home-root .\proj --data-root .\proj\.openminion cron create --instruction "say hi" --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" --tz Europe/Rome --json
& .venv\Scripts\openminion.exe --home-root .\proj --data-root .\proj\.openminion cron create --instruction "say hi" --at 2026-12-31T09:00:00+00:00 --json
```

## Expected

All three jobs are created (`"ok": true`).

## Actual

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `--cron "0 9 * * 1-5"` (no `--tz`) | `ok: false`, `Invalid schedule: unknown timezone: UTC` |
| `--cron ... --tz UTC` | `ok: false`, `Invalid schedule: unknown timezone: UTC` |
| `--cron ... --tz Europe/Rome` | `ok: false`, `Invalid schedule: unknown timezone: Europe/Rome` |
| `--at 2026-12-31T09:00:00+00:00` | `ok: true` |

After `pip install tzdata` in the same venv, `--cron ... --tz Europe/Rome` returns `ok: true` with a task id.

## Impact

- Scheduled tasks (`cron create`, and the model-facing `task.schedule` with `{kind: "cron"}`) are unusable on Windows out of the box, with an error that points at the user's input rather than a missing dependency.
- Users following the docs' `--tz` examples hit it immediately.

## Suggested fix

Add `tzdata; sys_platform == "win32"` (or unconditionally) to `project.dependencies`, or catch `ZoneInfoNotFoundError` and say "install tzdata".

## Notes

Found by MinionProbe probe `tasks.cron_schedules` (CLI only, no model calls).

---
Found with [MinionProbe](https://github.com/AliceMessi/minionprobe), a building-block probe suite for OpenMinion built for Cortensor Hackathon #5.

title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl' — sync_lock() breaks every subcommand on Windows
body:
### Describe the bug

`state.py::sync_lock()` does an unconditional `import fcntl` inside the function body. `fcntl` is POSIX-only, so on Windows the very first call that touches the lock raises `ModuleNotFoundError` and the command dies before doing any work.

Every subcommand that persists state hits it, so this is not limited to one path — `freemodels list` fails immediately, and `sync` / `install-cron` fail the same way.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the plugin on Windows (`hermes plugins install GoSlowPoke168/hermes-openrouter-free-rotator`, then enable it).
2. Run any subcommand:
   ```
   hermes freemodels list
   ```
3. Observe:
   ```
   File "...\state.py", line 118, in sync_lock
       import fcntl
   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'
   ```

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Python: 3.14.7 (win32-x64)
- Hermes data dir on a Windows-native path (`C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\hermes`)

### Suggested fix

Keep the POSIX path byte-for-byte identical and add an `msvcrt` fallback for the lock only — the semantics needed are the same (exclusive, non-blocking, `False` when another run holds it):

```python
@contextmanager
def sync_lock():
    path = state_dir() / "sync.lock"
    try:
        import fcntl
    except ImportError:
        fcntl = None  # Windows: msvcrt below

    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        if fcntl is None:
            import msvcrt

            # msvcrt.locking locks a byte range, so the file needs at least
            # one byte and the handle must sit at offset 0.
            if fh.seek(0, 2) == 0:
                fh.write("\0")
                fh.flush()
            fh.seek(0)
            try:
                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
            except OSError:
                yield False
                return
            try:
                yield True
            finally:
                fh.seek(0)
                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
            return

        try:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError:
            yield False
            return
        try:
            yield True
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
```

This is the patch currently running locally on Windows — `hermes freemodels list`, `sync`, `status`, `pin` and `unpin` all pass with it in place, and `sync` wrote the expected config changes.

### A related Windows gap: `install-cron`

`croninstall.py` shells out to `crontab`, which does not exist on Windows (Git Bash / MSYS has no cron). `install_cron_line()` calls `subprocess.run(["crontab", ...])`, which raises `FileNotFoundError` on such a host. Not part of this patch, but worth knowing about — the `hermes` cron scheduler is the working equivalent there.

Happy to open a PR for the `sync_lock` change if you'd prefer it as a diff.

title: POSIX cron .py scripts lose the generation environment (ModuleNotFoundError)
body:
On POSIX, a cron job whose script is Python and imports a third-party library fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` even though the same script runs fine by hand.

`cron/scheduler_script.py` → `_windows_cron_python_invocation()`: the Windows branch builds a `PYTHONPATH` overlay (repo root + generation site-packages), the POSIX branch returns `{}`. The launcher starts the managed store Python with `PYTHONPATH` popped, and that interpreter carries only Hermes itself, so every cron `.py` with third-party imports has to re-add the paths by hand — a maintenance trap that breaks on each environment migration.

Fix (PR to follow): mirror the Windows overlay on POSIX, gated on the generation environment existing. PR: _linked below_.

title: check_project_complete blocks completion: hermes_cli not importable in cron context
body:
## Bug: `check_project_complete` blocks project completion — `hermes_cli` not importable in cron context

**Repo:** `yzy806806/agora`
**Affected:** `agora/kanban_compat.py` (`_build_bridge`), `agora/leader_loop.py` (`check_project_complete`), `leader_heartbeat.sh`

### Symptom

Leader outputs `PROJECT_COMPLETE` repeatedly (128× in one observed project), but `complete_count` stays 0 and `status` remains `active` forever. The completion gate never fires.

### Root Cause

`check_project_complete` reads the board via `kanban_compat.py` → `importlib.import_module("hermes_cli.kanban_db")` **at module load time**. `hermes_cli` lives in the Hermes core tree (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/`) and is only importable when the interpreter has `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` on `sys.path` (the gateway does `sys.path.insert(0, .../hermes-agent)`).

The cron script (`leader_heartbeat.sh` → tools-python) does **not** set that up. So the import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` → `check_project_complete` catches it → `_board_read=False` → **fail-closed: `complete_count` reset to 0** (by design, v2.0.10 CHANGELOG). Because the board read **permanently** fails in the cron context, the 2-consecutive-signal counter never reaches 2 → completion is blocked.

**Verified:** With `PYTHONPATH=~/.hermes/hermes-agent` + full plugin import path → `board read OK`. Without → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'`.

### Why not a bypass

Hermes docs are explicit: *"Both surfaces route through the same `kanban_db` layer, so reads see a consistent view and writes can't drift."* A raw `sqlite3` bypass in `leader_loop.py` would break that guarantee. The fail-closed mechanism is correct and should stay; the bug is only that the read never succeeds in the cron context.

### Proposed universal fix (in `agora/kanban_compat.py`, no env workaround)

Add an import-discovery step **before** `_build_bridge()` that finds `hermes_cli` independently of `PYTHONPATH`:

```python
def _ensure_hermes_cli_importable() -> None:
    """Make `hermes_cli` importable for standalone/cron interpreters.

    The gateway inserts <hermes-home>/hermes-agent onto sys.path; a bare
    interpreter (leader_heartbeat.sh cron, dashboard shim) does not, so the
    bridge's importlib.import_module("hermes_cli.kanban_db") raises
    ModuleNotFoundError and check_project_complete fails closed on every
    heartbeat. Discover the core tree and add it to sys.path once.
    """
    try:
        import hermes_cli  # noqa: F401
        return
    except ImportError:
        pass
    import os, sys
    from pathlib import Path
    cands = []
    if os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME"):
        cands.append(Path(os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]) / "hermes-agent")
    # kanban_compat.py is <hermes-home>/plugins/agora/agora/kanban_compat.py
    cands.append(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "hermes-agent")
    for c in cands:
        if (c / "hermes_cli" / "__init__.py").is_file():
            p = str(c)
            if p not in sys.path:
                sys.path.insert(0, p)
            return
```

Call it at module top: `_ensure_hermes_cli_importable()` before `kanban_db = _build_bridge()`.

**Why universal:**
- Plugin-internal, not env-dependent — works in every install (gateway, cron, dashboard, standalone) without per-host `PYTHONPATH` patching
- Respects the documented design — still goes through `hermes_cli.kanban_db` (consistency guarantee intact), no sqlite3 bypass
- Fail-safe — if discovery finds nothing, behaviour is unchanged (import raises, fail-closed)
- Two sources (env `HERMES_HOME` + plugin-relative `parents[3]`) → robust against relocation

### Secondary hardening (optional, separate PR)

The 2-consecutive counter is fragile: it advances only when the **byte window** (since `complete_check_pos`) contains the exact string `PROJECT_COMPLETE`, else reset. In one project: 180 sessions, only 84 (47%) with the token → two consecutive token-bearing windows are rare. Suggestion: anchor detection on **`sess

title: [BUG] PM runtime: restart-safe cron external worker dies with ModuleNotFoundError: ruamel
body:
# [BUG] Restart-safe cron external worker dies on PM runtime: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ruamel'`

## Summary

Since the PM/managed-runtime migration, every cron job dispatched by a systemd-managed gateway fails before it starts: the external worker is spawned with `sys.executable -m cron.scheduler` in a sanitized environment, and under the PM runtime that interpreter is the **bare store Python**, which ships no third-party packages. The sanitizer strips the activated environment's site-packages from `PYTHONPATH`, then `pin_hermes_tree_on_pythonpath()` re-pins only the checkout root — so the worker imports `hermes_yaml` → `ruamel.yaml` and dies before it can acknowledge the handoff.

Every scheduled job in both of my profiles failed for ~9.5 hours (106 failed executions) until I hot-fixed it locally.

## Environment

- Version: 0.21.5 (git install, commit `346c14a9c5`; still reproducible on `origin/main` @ `cda237464a` — `git diff HEAD origin/main -- cron/` is empty)
- Install: PM/managed runtime — interpreter `/home/<user>/.hermes/tools/python-3.14.7+…/bin/python3` (site-packages holds only `pip`)
- Dependencies: `/home/<user>/.hermes/installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages`, activated in-process by `pm.environments.activate_dependencies()` which also sets `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = repo_root:site_packages`
- Gateway: systemd user unit (`INVOCATION_ID` set) → `restart_safe_gateway_child_argv()` returns `scoped`/`degraded`, i.e. always an external worker

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Worker command exactly as spawned (cron/scheduler.py:: _launch_external_cron_worker)
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin \
  PYTHONPATH=/home/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent \
  /home/<user>/.hermes/tools/python-3.14.7+…/bin/python3 -m cron.scheduler --help
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 194, in _run_module_as_main
  ...
  File ".../hermes_yaml.py", line 10, in <module>
    from ruamel.yaml import YAML
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ruamel'
```

```bash
# 2. Same command with the runtime site-packages re-added → works (exit 0)
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin \
  PYTHONPATH="/home/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent:/home/<user>/.hermes/installs/<key>/environments/<gen>/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages" \
  …/bin/python3 -m cron.scheduler --help   # exit 0
```

## Root cause chain

1. `cron/scheduler.py::_launch_external_cron_worker` builds `command = [sys.executable, "-m", "cron.scheduler", …]` — correct while `sys.executable` was the in-tree venv (deps included), wrong once the gateway runs on the store Python.
2. `environments/local.py::build_subprocess_env()` → `local_pythonpath.py::_strip_hermes_owned_pythonpath()` removes the runtime site-packages entry (it is recognised as Hermes-owned via `_validated_runtime_venv`).
3. `cron/scheduler_worker_env.py::pin_hermes_tree_on_pythonpath()` re-pins **only** the checkout root, so third-party imports are gone. The docstring documents dropping runtime site-packages deliberately (cross-version C-extension hazard for *user* children) — but this child *is* Hermes, running the *same* interpreter.

## Suggested fix

In `pin_hermes_tree_on_pythonpath()` (same reasoning as the repo-root pin — the worker is Hermes itself and shares `sys.executable`, so there is no cross-version hazard), also re-add the committed PM environment:

```python
from pm.environments import committed_venv, site_packages
environment = committed_venv(repo_root)
if environment:
    site.addsitedir(str(site_packages(environment)))   # addsidedir, not append: .pth members
```

`pm.environments` is stdlib-only by contract, so it is safe to import at this point. Alternative: have the worker run through the launcher/bootstrap instead of bare `-m`.

## Workaround (not in-tree)

`~/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/usercustomize.py` that re-activates the committed environment **only when a Hermes checkout is already on `sys.path`** (i.e. exactly this wo

title: [scanner] 🐛 wrapper: docker/podman run uses -it unconditionally, fails headless (not a TTY)
body:
## Summary

`scripts/contribute-wrapper.sh.in` (and therefore the generated `Formula/contribute.rb` wrapper) runs Docker/Podman with `-it` unconditionally:

```bash
docker_like_run() {
  local engine="$1"
  local -a args=(run --rm -it --name "${HIVE_CONTAINER_NAME:-hive-contributor}")
```

When stdin is not a terminal — the relay started from a systemd user unit, a launchd agent, `nohup … &`, cron, or any CI job — Docker refuses to start: `the input device is not a TTY`, and Podman fails the same way. A contributor relay is exactly the kind of long-lived process people run headless, and on macOS (where Docker/Podman is the default runtime for this wrapper) there is no Apptainer fallback, so the wrapper is unusable as a service there.

The Apptainer path is not affected (no TTY flag).

## Fix

Allocate a TTY only when one is present, keep stdin attached either way:

```bash
local -a args=(run --rm -i --name "${HIVE_CONTAINER_NAME:-hive-contributor}")
[[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]] && args+=(-t)
```

Add a case to `scripts/test_generate_formula.py` asserting the rendered wrapper does not contain `run --rm -it` (the existing placeholder-substitution test shows the pattern).

## Related

A smaller robustness issue in the same file: `collect_env_names` parses `env` line-by-line (`env | while IFS='=' read -r name _`), so an exported variable whose value contains a newline followed by text starting with an allowed prefix (`HIVE_…`, `AGENT_…`, …) yields a bogus "name" and `export "APPTAINERENV_${name}=${!name}"` aborts the wrapper under `set -u` ("invalid indirect expansion"). `lima_run` already uses `compgen -e`; `collect_env_names` should too. Worth fixing in the same PR.

title: [Bug]: v0.23.0 Docker image, headless ARM64 (Pi 4 / Debian 13): gateway self-exits every ~60-68 s — "Input is not a terminal (fd=0)" — profile reconcile loop
body:
### Bug Description

The gateway starts fully (warm-up ok, api_server listening on 127.0.0.1:8642, 1 platform, "Model context warmed: <model> -> 1048576 tokens", "Press Ctrl+C to stop"), then self-exits ~17-68 s after start. The shutdown is graceful but initiated by a SIGTERM from its own s6-supervise parent; it exits with code 1 — the documented self-revive mechanism (ref issue #42675) — and the container/profile boot flow restarts it, indefinitely (40+ reconcile cycles logged, one every ~68 s, prior_exit=clean).

Key observation for headless operation: when running the gateway in the foreground of a non-TTY exec, it prints and shuts down:
    Warning: Input is not a terminal (fd=0).
    Shutting down… (finalizing session)
The new embedded-UI gateway appears to require an interactive terminal — a headless Docker container never has one. Agent-side chats are consequently cut mid-turn: "Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown."


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Host: Raspberry Pi 4 (aarch64), Debian 13, Docker 29.9.2, headless (stdin not a TTY).
2. Official image nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.23.0 (linux/arm64 confirmed via docker inspect), HERMES_HOME = named volume mounted at /opt/data.
3. Model provider: OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint pointing at a local Ollama container — provider: "ollama" (alias of "custom"), base_url: "http://ollama:11434/v1", model.default: "glm-5.3-flash:cloud" (Ollama account signed in, cloud model pulled).
   No messaging platforms configured.
4. `docker compose up -d hermes-agent` → gateway starts fully, then self-exits within ~17-68 s (restart loop).
5. Foreground probe (non-TTY exec): docker compose exec -T hermes-agent hermes gateway run --no-supervise
   → prints "Warning: Input is not a terminal (fd=0). Shutting down… (finalizing session)", then exits.


### Expected Behavior

The gateway runs indefinitely in headless Docker (stdin not a TTY), serving the api_server/webapp/dashboard — the normal, supported state for the official Docker image.


### Actual Behavior

Gateway fully boots and warms, then receives SIGTERM from s6-supervise within ~17-68 s, exits with code 1 (self-revive by design, ref issue #42675), and the loop repeats indefinitely (40+ profile-reconcile cycles; docker restart count > 20).
Interactive TUI chats are cut mid-turn ("Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown").
Ruled out: OOM (gateway heartbeat RSS ~183 MB, host 3.8 GB total / 3.2 GB available, dmesg clean, oom=false); provider unreachable (both /v1/models and /api/tags return HTTP 200 from inside the container; a direct `ollama run <cloud-model>` completes in 1.3-2.7 s).
The loop reproduces with image-default config as well (provider "auto", base_url unset).


### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
2026-11-08 06:00:48,391 INFO gateway.run: Turn machinery warmed in 6.4s (21 tool schema(s) materialized)
2026-11-08 06:00:48,457 INFO gateway.run: Press Ctrl+C to stop

2026-11-08 06:00:48,488 INFO gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: kanban.max_in_progress unset; using memory-derived default max_in_progress=7 (set kanban.max_in_progress in config.yaml to override)
2026-11-08 06:00:48,648 INFO gateway.run: Cron scheduler will tick 1 profile(s): ['default']
2026-11-08 06:00:48,690 INFO gateway.run: Gateway housekeeping started (interval=60s)
2026-11-08 06:00:53,502 INFO gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: embedded in gateway (interval=60.0s)
2026-11-08 06:01:05,936 INFO gateway.run: Received SIGTERM — initiating shutdown
2026-11-08 06:01:05,937 WARNING gateway.run: Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=no parent_pid=170 parent_name=s6-supervise loadavg_1m=1.27
2026-11-08 06:01:05,946 INFO gateway.run: Stopping gateway...
2026-11-08 06:01:06,202 INFO gateway.run: Shutdown phase: notify_active_sessio

title: feat(security): interactive approval policy for dangerous operations
body:
### Problem
Autonomous model agents can propose potentially destructive or irreversible actions (e.g. `git push`, deleting files, running package managers, making outbound network requests, executing commands outside workspace). There is currently no interactive human-in-the-loop approval gate to intercept and validate these actions before execution.

### Objective
Implement an approval policy mechanism that intercepts high-risk tool proposals and requests interactive operator confirmation or applies configured authorization policies.

### Scope & Requirements
1. **High-Risk Operation Classification**:
   - Classify tools and operations into risk tiers:
     - High risk: `git push`, file deletions, outbound network requests, arbitrary package installations (`pip`, `npm`, `cargo`), shell commands targeting paths outside workspace.
     - Low risk: read-only operations (`read_file`, `git status`, `git diff`).
2. **Approval Modes**:
   - `prompt`: Interactive CLI / TUI prompt asking user for explicit authorization (yes/no/always allow for session).
   - `deny`: Automatically reject high-risk operations with a permission error.
   - `allow`: Permit without interactive confirmation (for non-interactive headless or sandboxed automation).
3. **Headless & Automation Safety**:
   - Automatically fallback to `deny` or configured non-interactive policy when stdin is not a TTY (CI, cron runs, automated benchmarks).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement approval interception layer in `crates/cortex-runtime/src/agent.rs` and `crates/cortex-core/src/permissions.rs`.
- [ ] Support approval configuration in `~/.cortex/settings.json` and agent YAML manifests.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests covering approval prompts, allowances, and rejections.
- [ ] Update `docs/architecture/sandbox.md` and `SECURITY.md`.

title: batch: run stalls silently on an interactive write confirmation, and says nothing while it waits
body:
Found while running the first `code-small` batch (finance-hub #48, batch `0008-rung3-t48`) on 2026-11-06.

## What happened

`mypi-batch run 0008-rung3-t48` started at 17:28:35. From the terminal the human sees nothing: no progress line, no workspace name, no pane id. The supervisor was working in a herdr workspace the driver had just created (`mypi-b-0008-rung3-t48-t48`), where pi was asking:

```
 This run wants to write files.
 write /Users/afshin/.../run-details/plan.md

 → Yes
   No
```

It sat on that dialog for four minutes until a human ran `herdr pane send-keys w2E:p1 Enter`. The supervisor then wrote `plan.md`, sent `INTENT_TO_MODIFY` and the `WORK_ORDER`, and both peers started. Left alone, `run.timeout_minutes: 30` (finance-hub `mypi-batch.yaml`) would have ended the ticket at about 17:58 having spent money and done no work.

Two independent reasons the human cannot answer:

1. `run` prints only one line per ticket, after `runBatch` returns (`src/batch/cli.ts`). Nothing names the workspace or pane it created, so the run is silent for its entire duration.
2. The question is asked by the supervisor pi inside another herdr workspace. Nothing in the terminal says a question exists, and the dialog is invisible unless the human switches workspace and finds the pane.

For an unattended run — cron, overnight, CI — this is not a slow run, it is a run that cannot start.

## Peers are blocked outright, and the block is partial

The implementer's `FINAL_REPORT` on the first work order, at 17:34, quoted from `run-details/conversation.jsonl`:

> Every write channel is blocked in this session: `edit`, `write`, and `bash` commands that modify files all return `Write blocked (no confirmation UI available)`.

That string is `write-guard.ts`'s own block reason, so the guard does load inside the peer session (`src/peer/peer-main.ts:177`). With `hasUI: false` the guard can never be satisfied — `approved` is only ever set by a confirming human — so **every** write for the life of the peer is blocked. A batch run cannot succeed on a machine with this extension installed, whatever the human answers for the supervisor.

The block is also partial, which is worse than a clean block. `bashWrites` does not match `perl -pi -e`, so the implementer patched through that hole, and `exit()` inside `perl -p` truncated the file: `src/components/portfolio/HoldingsTable.tsx` went to 0 bytes (HEAD still held the 9915-byte blob). The supervisor restored it in the same turn (`git diff` clean at 17:35), so the branch survived, but a blocked peer can still damage the tree.

## Costs, as measured

Supervisor $0.094, implementer $0.019, and the ticket produced no code. The 30-minute deadline would have been the ceiling for a run that was never going to finish.

## What a run should print

Today the only output is one line per ticket, after `runBatch` returns. Running it by hand should show the run: a start block before it waits, one line per real event, a named line when something is waiting for a human, and the same final line it prints now. Every value below already exists at the point it is printed — `createWorkspace` returns the pane id, the poll loop in `src/batch/executor.ts` already stats `run-details/`, and `conversation.jsonl` already carries `AGENT_REGISTER`, `WORK_ORDER`, `INTENT_TO_MODIFY` and `FINAL_REPORT`.

17:34 implementer: FINAL_REPORT NOT DONE — writes blocked (no confirmation UI)
17:35 supervisor: restored src/components/portfolio/HoldingsTable.tsx from HEAD

18:02 48  failure  exit 1  ...
```

comments.body:
Landed in `e9c612e`, main check green: https://github.com/afshinator/mypy-multi-agent/actions/runs/42326199096 (1541 passed, 2 skipped; web 57).

What `run` prints now:

- **Start block, before it waits** — batch, ticket, slug; worktree, `branch task/<slug>`, base commit; supervisor pane id with `watch: herdr pane read <pane>`; deadline clock time.
- **One line per event** as `conversation.jsonl` grows: `AGENT_REGISTER`, `WORK_ORDER`, `INTENT_TO_MODIFY`, `FINAL_REPORT` (headline only), each with the event's own timestamp. `EventTail` keeps an offset, so a poll never reprints the transcript and a half-written line waits for its newline.
- **The line this run needed** — when the pane shows a confirmation: `<pane> is waiting for input: "<question>" — press Enter there (herdr pane send-keys <pane> Enter)`. The question is read from the transcript above the `→ Yes` choice (`questionInPane`), only when `herdr pane get` reports `blocked`.
- **A stall is an outcome** — `supervisor-stalled`, never `timeout`: detail is `waiting for input in <pane>: <question>` when a question is open, `no run event for <ms> ms` when the run has gone quiet. The window is a quarter of the ticket budget floored at a minute, derived from the same knob. A run that never emits a single event stays `timeout` — there is no progress baseline to be late from.
- **`--quiet`** keeps the old surface: one line per ticket, no progress.

Unattended by construction: the supervisor is launched with `MYPY_UNATTENDED=1`,

One more fact from the live run, because it changes what a fix can rely on: **herdr was never opened as a UI.** The human launched `mypi-batch run` in a plain terminal with no herdr window attached. The driver still worked — it talks to the herdr *server* (a daemon, up since 27 Oct, independent of any window) — so panes were created and agents ran in a session nobody was looking at. There was no way to click "Yes" not because the dialog was hidden but because the only surface that could show it was never on screen.

That means the printed line cannot be a nicety. `run` has to be the channel: pane id, the question text, and the exact `herdr pane send-keys <pane> Enter` to answer it — which is what `e9c612e` now prints. It also means a batch must be able to finish with no herdr UI anywhere, which is what `MYPY_UNATTENDED=1` gives the supervisor and the peers.

Leftover state from that run, for whoever picks this up: after the CLI was Ctrl-C'd, two peer processes outlived it (PIDs 71617 and 73930, one of them started by the retry path at 17:35). The supervisor's pi had exited, so nothing owned them. They have been killed. The herdr workspace `mypi-b-0008-rung3-t48-t48` (w2E) and the worktree `../ma-wt-b-0008-rung3-t48-t48` are untouched: the worktree's run-details hold the peer report quoted above, and its tree is clean at `e20fe33`.

Worth a separate ticket if you agree: a killed run leaves orphan peers behind, and `run` should reap them when the supervisor's pane is gone.

The orphan-peer gap is fixed rather than filed: `937c784`, main check green — https://github.com/afshinator/mypy-multi-agent/actions/runs/42328238228.

`run` now reaps a run's peers by the only string that names that run and no other: its own `run-details` path, which every peer carries in its command line as the `--config` file. Twice: once before an attempt (so a run killed earlier is cleared before a new one adds more) and once in the `finally`, after the workspace closes, so this attempt's peers never outlive it. `pkill` matching nothing is the ordinary case and is not an error; when it did kill something the run prints `killed peers left behind by an earlier attempt`.

Two tests: one asserts the exact pattern passed to `pkill` is the absolute run-details path (not a bare `peer-main`, which would kill another run's peers) and that "nothing matched" is not a failure; the other drives a ticket to its end and asserts the reaper is called with that run's path on the failing path too, and that the notice is printed when it killed something.

Not covered by this: a run whose CLI is `SIGKILL`ed and that is never re-run leaves its peers until someone kills them — the sweep happens on the next attempt at that run.

Also of note for anyone running `bun run check` locally: the full-tree lint exits 1 with `Found 1 error`, pointing at `test/unit/web-tool.test.ts:126`, which is a warning when that file is checked alone and passes with `--max-diagnostics=500`. It is the biome diagnostic

Live evidence, third attempt, and the first one that needed no keystroke anywhere.

`mypi-batch run 0008-rung3-t48` (finance-hub #48) printed exactly the shape this ticket asked for:

```

  worktree /Users/afshin/Documents/dev/ma-wt-b-0008-rung3-t48-t48  branch task/b-0008-rung3-t48-t48  base main
  supervisor pane w2G:p1 — watch: herdr pane read w2G:p1
  deadline 18:52:52

18:22:54 implementer registered (deepseek/deepseek-flash)
18:22:54 reviewer registered (openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna)
18:24:21 supervisor -> implementer: work order task-1
18:24:43 implementer: intent to modify bash
18:25:22 implementer: FINAL_REPORT FINAL
18:26:55 supervisor -> reviewer: work order task-2
18:27:29 reviewer: FINAL_REPORT Standards: clean. Spec: clean. No blocking issue.

The peers wrote code this time: `HoldingsTable.tsx` 10 lines, `holdings-table.test.tsx` +74. That is the evidence DoD 7 wanted — a work order and a peer change with nobody touching a pane — and it also proves the `peerCommandFor` fix, because the first two attempts died at exactly that point.

Two defects found by this run, neither of them #48's:

1. **The gate is worktree-hostile in the target repo.** The run ended `failure exit 1 status failure` on `gate-rejected: bun run check`. Running that command myself in the same worktree: 851 of 853 pass, one fails — `tests/scripts/worktree.test.ts > assertMainCheckout > returns the realpath of the main

Status, so nobody re-derives it:

- **The target-repo cause is owned elsewhere.** finance-hub#51 (the worktree-hostile test) is being fixed by another agent, so the rung-3 run's `failure` should become a real `success` on the next attempt, with no change here.
- **The driver-side consequence is split out** as #419: a gate that cannot pass in a worktree currently reads as a failure of the branch, and it costs the whole run before anyone learns which it was.

So this ticket's remaining work is exactly two things: nothing on the peer-write path (that is proven — the guard fix and `peerCommandFor` both exercised live), and the `scorecard-write-failed: ENOENT … /quality/ledger.jsonl` noted above, which is a supervisor artifact-path bug and not yet its own ticket.

Not done here, listed rather than hidden: the `?: ERROR` mapping is #419 item 4, and the retry path (`RETRY` events printing as `?: RETRY`) is still unlabelled for the same reason.

The `scorecard-write-failed` finding recorded above now has a fix: `fd27862`, main check green — https://github.com/afshinator/mypy-multi-agent/actions/runs/42413648943.

Verified first, then fixed:

- The failure is real and repeatable, not noise: `{"type":"ERROR","event":"scorecard-write-failed","message":"ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Users/afshin/Documents/dev/ma-wt-b-0011-rung4-t42-t42/quality/ledger.jsonl'"}`. It fired on every batch run, because `workspaceRoot` is the throwaway worktree and `src/scorecard/collector.ts:74` does a bare `appendFile` with no `mkdir`.
- `mkdir` would not have been a fix: a line in the worktree dies with the checkout on success. The card reaches the ledger by the documented route — the driver copies `run-details/scorecard.json` out (`executor.ts`), and `collect` reads `<root>/run-details/scorecard.json` (`src/scorecard/collector.ts:53`). Both batch runs' copies are present.
- The fix is one guard: append only when `<workspaceRoot>/quality` exists (`src/runtime/runtime.ts:844-846`). No directory is created in a repo that keeps no ledger, and nothing that was going to survive is lost.

Tests: a new case in `test/integration/scorecard.test.ts` asserts the card still lands and no `quality/` is created. I checked it is red-capable by removing the guard — it fails with exactly the production `ENOENT` and a created `quality/` — then restored it. The existing ledger test (line appended when the directory exists) still passes; 1554 passed

title: Output layer: versioned envelope and error taxonomy
body:
## Why

ADR-0004: the output contract is the product. The moment a cron job or an agent
parses this, it is an API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Versioned envelope on every success payload
- [ ] JSON when stdout is not a TTY, rich table when it is, `--output csv`
- [ ] `--output` explicitly overrides TTY detection
- [ ] Errors to stderr as JSON with a stable code and nonzero exit
- [ ] Full error taxonomy implemented per ADR-0004
- [ ] Golden-file tests for each renderer
- [ ] `CliRunner` tests asserting exact JSON shape

## Out of scope

The `health` block inside errors (separate issue).

## Dependencies

Blocked by scaffolding. Blocks all command issues.

## Notes

Adding an error code later is an API change — get the taxonomy right here.

comments.body:
🤖 **Decision for U5: a malformed config file gets its own taxonomy code, `CONFIG_INVALID`.**

#31 (config, U3) raised this and left a deliberate seam: `ConfigError.code` is `None` because ADR-0004 has no code for an unreadable config, and `LEAGUE_NOT_FOUND` would be actively wrong — it tells an agent to retry with a different `--league`, which cannot work when the file itself will not parse.

Uncoded is the wrong resting place. The taxonomy exists so an agent knows what to do next, and "your config file is broken, fix the file, retrying will not help" is a different instruction from every availability or throttling code we have. Rendering it generically invites a retry loop.

`CLAUDE.md` rule 4 is right that adding a code is an API change. That is an argument for doing it **now**: the package is `0.1.0.dev0`, nothing is published, and no consumer parses the taxonomy yet. This is the cheapest moment it will ever have.

So, in U5:

1. Amend **ADR-0004** to add `CONFIG_INVALID` — user-fixable, not retryable, distinct from `LEAGUE_NOT_FOUND`.
2. Give `ConfigError` that code and drop the `None` seam and its comment in `config/leagues.py`.
3. Cover it like every other code: a test that produces it and asserts the exit status, and one asserting it is distinguishable from the credential, availability, and throttling causes.

The other two decisions in #31 stand as made. Tolerating unknown top-level keys while rejecting unknown keys inside `[leagues.<name>]` is the right split — ARCH

🤖 One more decision for U5, from #36. That PR put an error's remediation text in `details["remediation"]` rather than promoting it to a top-level payload key, deliberately, because adding one is an ADR-0004 contract change and a refactor is the wrong place to make it quietly.

**U5 should promote it.** Remediation is the part an agent acts on. Leaving it in a general-purpose bag makes reading it optional, which means some consumers will not, and the whole point of the taxonomy is that a failure tells the caller what to do next. Make it a first-class envelope field, amend ADR-0004 in the same PR, and cover it like every other contract field.

If you disagree after reading #36, say so in the PR body rather than silently keeping it in `details` — either answer is defensible, an undocumented one is not. — posted from host Johns-MacBook-Air-3

title: Cron-Läufe lesen die lokale Override-Datei nicht (SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL fehlt in cron.env)
body:
### Ziel

`entrypoint.sh` schreibt in Zeile 6 mit `export -p > /app/cron.env` die Umgebung für die Cron-Jobs fest. Den Standardpfad der Override-Datei (`SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL=/data/config.local.yaml`) setzt das Skript aber erst danach, und nur im Block für das Web-Passwort. Deshalb lesen Bot und Web die Override-Datei, die Cron-Läufe (`discover` 07:30, `audit --check-adopted` 06:45, `scout` 18:00, Kaufliste sonntags) aber nicht. Das gilt, solange die Variable nicht von Hand in der `.env` steht.

Folgen:
- Änderungen aus dem Web-Konfigeditor wirken im täglichen Lauf nicht.
- Accounts, die per Curator-Mining-Button zu `search.followed_users` kommen, wirken dort ebenfalls nicht.
- `rekordbox.path_map` steht laut `BETRIEB.md` nur in der Override-Datei. Der tägliche Lauf schreibt die Rekordbox-XML deshalb ohne diese Zuordnung.

Dieses Issue setzt den Standardpfad am Anfang von `entrypoint.sh`, vor `export -p`, und zwar unabhängig vom Web-Passwort. Danach sehen Cron, Bot und Web dieselbe Override-Datei. Ein von Hand gesetzter, nicht leerer Wert bleibt erhalten.

### Betroffene Dateien

- `entrypoint.sh`: vor `export -p > /app/cron.env` die Zeile `export SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL="${SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL:-/data/config.local.yaml}"`, mit Kommentar zum Warum (Cron sieht nur, was vor `export -p` gesetzt ist). Die gleichlautende Zeile im Web-Block bleibt stehen, `tests/acceptance/test_issue_172.py` prüft sie. Den Kommentar darüber anpassen: Die Variable ist schon gesetzt, die Zeile ist nur noch Absicherung.
- `docker-compose.yml`: nur den Kommentar in Zeile 25–27 an das neue Verhalten anpassen (gilt für alle Prozesse, nicht nur für den Editor).
- `BETRIEB.md`: im Abschnitt mit `SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL` (bei `rekordbox.path_map`) einen Satz ergänzen: Die Override-Datei gilt auch für die Cron-Läufe. Prüfen lässt sich das mit `docker compose exec sc-digger grep -c SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL /app/cron.env` (Ergebnis 1).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: eine Zeile unter „Unreleased“ → „Behoben“ (falls nicht vorhanden, anlegen) mit PR-Nummer
- `tests/acceptance/test_issue_<N>.py` (Akzeptanztests unten, zeichengenau)
- `tests/test_entrypoint_cron.py` (eigene Tests ergänzen, bestehende unverändert lassen)

Weitere Dateien dürfen nicht geändert werden.

### Schnittstellen

```python
# Keine Python-Schnittstelle. Verhalten von entrypoint.sh nach der Änderung:
#
# 1. Ganz oben, vor `export -p > /app/cron.env`:
#      export SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL="${SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL:-/data/config.local.yaml}"
#    Unabhängig davon, ob SC_DIGGER_WEB_PASSWORD gesetzt ist.
# 2. /app/cron.env enthält danach die Variable; `. /app/cron.env` setzt sie auf
#    - /data/config.local.yaml, wenn sie vorher fehlte oder leer war,
#    - den vorher gesetzten Wert sonst (z. B. /custom/local.yaml).
# 3. Bot (`exec python -m sc_digger.bot`) und Web (`python -m sc_digger.web …`) erben denselben Wert.
# 4. Alles andere (Cron-Einträge, install_crontab, Reihenfolge, Bot als letzter Befehl) bleibt unverändert.
```

### Nicht Teil dieser Aufgabe

- Kein Ausschalten über einen leeren Wert. Das Verhalten von `${VAR:-…}` bei leerem Wert bleibt. Ein eigener Schalter wäre ein eigenes Issue.
- Den Kaufliste-Cron-Eintrag (`Config.load('config.yaml')`) nicht umbauen. Er liest die Override-Datei über die Variable, sobald sie in `cron.env` steht.
- Keine Änderung an `sc_digger/models.py` (`Config.load`), `bot.py` oder `web/__main__.py`.
- Keine Änderung an `Dockerfile` oder an der `.env.example`.
- Keine neuen Cron-Einträge.

### Akzeptanztests

```python
"""Akzeptanztests: Cron-Läufe sehen dieselbe Override-Datei wie Bot und Web (SC_DIGGER_CONFIG_LOCAL)."""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

DEFAULT = "/data/config.local.yaml"
SH = shutil.which("sh")

title: Heartbeat app: alert when a scheduled job or script stops checking in
body:
**Goal**
As a team or admin, I want a Heartbeat app from the catalog that gives each of my jobs a check-in URL and alerts me when a check-in is missed, so that I hear about a silent cron failure anywhere on my infrastructure.

**Example**
I create a check "db-dump" expecting a ping every 24 h with 1 h grace. My server's cron curls its URL after each dump. When a night is missed, Slack gets one alert; when pings resume, one recovery message.

**Suggestion**
Folder `maintenance/heartbeat` in automaton-apps. A small web app (ping endpoint and a list of checks) plus an Action every 5 minutes that finds overdue checks. State in `AUTOMATON_APP_DATA_DIR`; webhook URL as a secret. Python standard library. Out of scope v1: email, teams, cron-expression schedules.

**Done when**
Installed from the Catalog on the test server: a check pinged on time stays green; a missed ping produces exactly one alert at a test webhook and one recovery message; check-in URLs are unguessable; no secret appears in logs. README documents it.

## Constat

`scripts/translation/check_twin_parity_changed.py` (`derive_candidate_pairs`, lignes 71-95) construit ses paires candidates par **suffixe de langue** (`_SUFFIX_RE` sur `TARGET_LANGS = ["en","es","ar","fa","zh","ru","pt"]`). Les paires `native-both` C#↔Python declarees dans `scripts/notebook_tools/twin_pairs.d/` ne sont **jamais candidates** : le garde incrémental rend « rien a verifier » → vert, puis le cron `twin-parity-cron.yml` rougit 24 h plus tard.

## Instance mesuree (PR #24869, 06/11)

- Paire `Z3-Python-04 Strings & Regex` (`parity_level: native-both`) : enrichissement markdown du jumeau C# seul (9 cellules de lecture).
- `twin-parity-guard` = SUCCESS au head — les 7 candidates derivees sont toutes `…-CSharp_en.ipynb`, `…-CSharp_es.ipynb`, etc. — **aucune** ne nomme `Z3-04-Strings-Regex-Python.ipynb`.
- Rejeu de la commande exacte du cron (`check_twin_parity.py --ci-strict --check`) : `drift_content=1`, rc=1. Le drift etait introduit par la PR, invisible au garde.

## Mecanisme

```python
# derive_candidate_pairs, lignes 85-94 :
suffix_match = ctp._SUFFIX_RE.match(stem)
if suffix_match and suffix_match.group("lang") in ctp.TARGET_LANGS:
    # jumeau xxx_en.ipynb modifie → candidate sa source
else:
    for lang in ctp.TARGET_LANGS:
        # source xxx.ipynb modifiee → candidate tous ses jumeaux _en/_es/...
```

Une paire `native-both` (`Z3-04-Strings-Regex-CSharp.ipynb` ↔ `Z3-04-Strings-Regex-Python.ipynb`) n'a aucun suffixe de langue reconnu → le `else` derive des candidats `…-CSharp_en.ipynb` etc. qui n'existent pas → filtre disque les ecarte → 0 paire a verifier → vert.

## Ce qui manque

Le garde incrémental devrait aussi consulter `scripts/notebook_tools/twin_pairs.d/*.yaml` pour les paires `native-both` dont un membre apparait dans le diff. Le registre declare les chemins exacts des deux membres — la consultation est triviale.

## Impact

Toute PR qui touche **un seul cote** d'une paire `native-both` enregistree passe le garde incrémental vert, puis rougit le cron 24 h plus tard. Actuellement 7 paires en drift sur main (#24853), dont certaines pourraient etre evitees par ce garde.

title: Turn on the 5-minute refresh cron on the VPS
body:
## Parent

[Spec: Move Lookout off Streamlit](https://github.com/stonematt/lookout/issues/66)

## What to build

The VPS (`ssh itri`; pass `-o RemoteCommand=none` for non-interactive commands) runs the refresh command every 5 minutes, and the cron becomes the only writer to Storj. Today the cron runs catchup once a day at 06:00 from the `live` checkout through a wrapper script. That is replaced. The VPS secrets already live at `~/.config/lookout/secrets.toml`, symlinked from both checkouts. The venv already runs a uv-managed Python 3.12 (done 2026-10-30; the old 3.10 venv is kept as `.venv-py310-bak` until this ticket closes). title: Move plaincron into @sanely/cron
body:
Move the code of [plaincron](https://github.com/adelrodriguez/plaincron/tree/83f77c15722579ad1a6d3a4b253c9bc185a662aa) into [`packages/cron`](https://github.com/adelrodriguez/sanely/tree/1bc4530478cfc815ad965667df5e9e959ba08dca/packages/cron), which holds the keel skeleton. ## Source

- Repository: `adelrodriguez/plaincron` at `83f77c1`.
- npm: `plaincron@0.1.0`.
- Open issues and pull requests: none.
- Pending changesets: none.
- Docs: `README.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `docs/`.

## Features to import

Preserve these features from the source commit above:

- Compile the defined cron-phrase language into exact standard five-field cron expressions.
- Support minute and hour intervals, daily times, day sets, monthly ordinals, shortcuts, and time windows.
- Provide compile-time validation with useful error messages, runtime parsing, `safeParse`, and strict-form guards.
- Reject cron phrases that cannot produce an exact cron expression. Preserve interval phase and exclude a window's end time.

- plaincron has one entry point and a Node.js 20.0.0 floor, the same as the skeleton. The parent issue suggests this package or humanspan for the first move.

title: HIGH: pm2 worker and cron never load .env.local — cron dies on "CRON_SECRET is required", worker spams Redis NOAUTH
body:
## What happens

`ecosystem.config.cjs` documents in its own header that `worker` and `cron` get their
environment from `--import ./scripts/load-env.mjs`, but neither `args` string passes it:

```cjs
{ name: 'worker', script: 'node_modules/.bin/tsx', args: 'worker.ts' }
{ name: 'cron',   script: 'node_modules/.bin/tsx', args: 'scripts/cron-scheduler.ts' }
```

`env_file: '.env.local'` is not a pm2 feature — pm2 ignores that key. So the two sidecar
processes start with whatever the shell happened to export.

Observed on a bare host with no exported env:

- `cron`: `FATAL: CRON_SECRET is required` at boot, then `max_restarts: 5` exhausted →
  status `errored` and it stays down. Nothing retries.
- `worker`: ~600 × `ReplyError: NOAUTH` — with `REDIS_URL` unset it falls back to
  `redis://localhost:6379` and talks to the real Redis unauthenticated.

## Why it survived CI

`deploy.yml` and the compose stack export env into the container, so the preload is only
needed on a host that starts pm2 directly — which is exactly what `AGENTS.md` describes for
the VM deploy.

## Fix

Add `--import ./scripts/load-env.mjs` to both `args`. Shipped in the PR that closes this
issue; verified by `pm2 reload` followed by `cron` returning `{"ok":true}` and zero
`NOAUTH` lines in the worker log.

## Secondary observation

`cron` has `max_restarts: 5` and **no** `restart_delay`, unlike `worker` (10 + 2 s). A
process that legitimately exits non-zero at boot therefore burns its whole restart budget
in a few seconds and needs manual `pm2 restart`. Consider `max_restarts: 10` and
`restart_delay: 2000` for symmetry, and a startup-config `FATAL` should not be retried at
all — it can never succeed without an operator.

comments.body:
Claiming this one (no comments, no open PR touching `ecosystem.config.cjs`, and the only recent edits to that file are #3271's, already merged).

Starting point read from the committed tree at `a0ff28abe`: the file's own header, lines 13-20, already states the policy — "every app below loads its environment itself … the two `tsx` processes (worker, cron) get it from the `--import ./scripts/load-env.mjs` preload, because tsx does not read .env* at all. Without the preload those processes start with an empty environment: cron died with FATAL: CRON_SECRET is required (5 restarts → errored) and the worker silently fell back to redis://localhost:6379" — while `args` for both of those apps (`:140`, `:175`) is the bare script path, and both still carry the `env_file: '.env.local'` key the same header admits is a PM2 no-op (`:146`, `:181`). So the config documents a fix it does not make, and a reader who trusts the header is the exact case #3251 describes.

Plan:
- `--import ./scripts/load-env.mjs` on both `tsx` apps' `args`, matching how `package.json` invokes every other guard/probe that needs env (`guard:vocab`, `probe:rls`, `db:deploy-migrate`, `sweep:superadmin-get` …).
- Drop the two `env_file` keys rather than leave a silently-ignored one next to a working preload — the misleading line is what let this survive.
- The secondary observation as its own change: `cron` goes to `max_restarts: 10` + `restart_delay: 2000`, matching `worker`, so a boot that legitimately exits non-zero

Fixed in #3414 (branch `fix/pm2-sidecar-env-preload-3251`, rebased on `a9880a314`).

The four things that were wrong, read off the committed tree:

1. **The preload was prose, not config.** Both `tsx` apps carried `args: 'worker.ts'` and
   `args: 'scripts/cron-scheduler.ts'`. The header of the same file said they got their environment
   from `--import ./scripts/load-env.mjs` — a flag that was not in either `args`. `tsx` reads no
   `.env*` file, so both sidecars started with an empty environment: cron on
   `FATAL: CRON_SECRET is required`, the worker on its `redis://localhost:6379` default, which is
   the NOAUTH spam in the title.
2. **Both apps advertised `env_file: '.env.local'`.** PM2 7.x accepts the key and ignores it (#1424
   said so, the header said so, the keys stayed). Removed.
3. **`cron` had no room to fail** — `max_restarts: 5`, no `restart_delay`, `min_uptime: 10s`: five
   restarts spent in seconds by the boot that exits at its own config audit, then `errored` until a
   human intervenes. Now worker's budget (`10` + `restart_delay: 2000`).
4. **The host-side overrides were missing on the sidecars, and #1 makes them load-bearing.** The
   header claims the loopback `REDIS_URL`/`S3_ENDPOINT` overrides "win over the file for all three
   apps"; only `web` had them. This VM's `.env.local` is the Docker stack's file, carrying
   `redis://redis` and `http://minio`. Before this fix the sidecars never read that file, so the
   missing overrides cost nothing — the wo

title: Unidentified daily node failure from caller/agent_interface; log carries no argv
body:
## What

A bare `/usr/local/bin/node` exits 1 daily at ~07:00 UTC from cwd `/opt/poise/caller/agent_interface" (16 occurrences, 2026-10-23 → 2026-11-07, 7–11s elapsed, 900s timeout, not killed). It is the only error incident in the workspace log besides the two provider-auth polls (#903, #904).

## Why it is unactionable

The recorded event has no command line: `configuredCommand` is just the executable, no argv/args (excluded from context as secret-bearing), no stderr, no stack beyond the `runFile` finish frame. There is no way to tell which script or maintenance task this is — Caller infrastructure, a scheduled job, or something else.

## Suggested fix

- Identify the 07:00 UTC caller (scheduler/cron/Caller maintenance) and record what it actually is.
- More generally: process-failure diagnostics need a non-secret way to identify the child (script basename, subcommand, or operation tag). Right now any failure through this path with suppressed stderr is undebuggable from the log, which defeats the single-source-of-truth goal (#905).

title: npm script check:declared-deps points at a script that does not exist
body:
## Summary

`package.json` defines `"check:declared-deps": "node scripts/check-declared-deps.js"`, but `scripts/check-declared-deps.js` is not in the repository. Running it fails with `Error: Cannot find module '.../scripts/check-declared-deps.js'`.

## Why it matters

The script name suggests exactly the guard that would have prevented the `node-cron` problem (a module required in `src/` but not declared in `package.json`). Contributors who try it get a crash, and anyone wiring it into CI would break the pipeline.

## Proposed fix

Implement the script: walk `src/**/*.js`, collect bare-specifier `require()` targets, ignore Node built-ins (`module.builtinModules`), and fail if a package is not in `dependencies` (or in `optionalDependencies` when the require is guarded by try/catch). `madge` is already a devDependency and can provide the dependency graph. Alternatively use `depcheck`. Add it to CI next to `migrate:check`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm run check:declared-deps` exists and exits non-zero for the current `node-cron` gap.
- After declaring `node-cron`, it exits 0.
- It runs in the CI lint job.

---
_Identified during a repository audit of `main` at commit a3ee0307 (2026-10-14)._

comments.body:

A deprecation is only a warning and doesn't stop the script, so the quarantine problem probably has another cause. Please post the full output of `mailwatch_quarantine_maint.php --clean` and tell us what exactly fails.

There is no output and it quits/ends very quickly leading me to believe it's instantly failing.  I have had to create a separate cron job to cleanup the quarantine folder after XX days as this was not doing it.

dr

I reproduced this on PHP 8.5.12 with MailWatch 1.2.29. The cleanup itself works on PHP 8.5. Your exact output (only the deprecation text, no newline, exit status 0) appears when the script gets an empty quarantine path, and that happens in two cases:

1. `DISTRIBUTED_SETUP` is `true` in `conf.php`: the script then doesn’t read `Quarantine Dir` from the MailScanner configuration;
2. a file in `/etc/MailScanner/conf.d/` has an empty `Quarantine Dir =` line.

Please post the output of:

```bash
grep DISTRIBUTED_SETUP /var/www/html/mailscanner/conf.php
grep -rni 'quarantine *dir' /etc/MailScanner/MailScanner.conf /etc/MailScanner/conf.d/
grep -A3 'function mailwatch_version' /var/www/html/mailscanner/functions.php
```

The last one tells us which MailWatch version you are running.

Either way it is a bug on our side. The fix makes the cron script read the local MailScanner configuration also in a distributed setup, and exit with a clear error and a non-zero status when it cannot open the quarantine directory.

One more question: by “the quarantine is not working” do you mean only this cleanup, or also viewing/releasing messages from the web UI?

Thanks, that confirms it: with `DISTRIBUTED_SETUP` set to `true`, the cleanup script never read `Quarantine Dir`. This is fixed on the `1.2` branch. To try the fix:

```bash
curl -o /usr/local/bin/mailwatch_quarantine_maint.php https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mailwatch/MailWatch/1.2/tools/Cron_jobs/mailwatch_quarantine_maint.php
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/mailwatch_quarantine_maint.php
/usr/local/bin/mailwatch_quarantine_maint.php --clean; echo "exit status: $?"
```

The web UI reaches each relay over XML-RPC at `http://<relay hostname>/mailscanner/rpcserver.php`. On the Ubuntu relays, check:

1. the PHP XML extension is installed (`php -m | grep -i '^xml$'`, package `php8.5-xml`);
2. `RPC_ALLOWED_CLIENTS` in the relay's `conf.php` includes the IP of the UI host;
3. `curl -i http://<relay hostname>/mailscanner/rpcserver.php` from the UI host does not return 404 or a connection error.

If it still fails, please post the error shown in the web UI and the relay's web server error log.

After setting up a couple of VMs to replicate your distributed setup, I found that the relays also cause the web UI problem. With `DISTRIBUTED_SETUP` set to `true`, a relay doesn't read its own `Quarantine Dir`, so it answers the UI's XML-RPC calls with an empty quarantine. This is fixed on the `1.2` branch, but you don't need the fix: the setting itself is wrong for a relay.

`DISTRIBUTED_SETUP` must be `true` only on a host that doesn't run MailScanner, like a UI-only host. On each relay, set it in `conf.php`:

```php
define('DISTRIBUTED_SETUP', false);
```

This fixes both the web UI and the cleanup script on 1.2.29. If your UI host also runs MailScanner, tell me: the messages quarantined on that host need the fix instead.

Also check these two points on each relay:

1. `display_errors` must be `Off` for the web server's PHP. With it `On`, PHP 8.5 prints a deprecation notice before the XML and the UI gets an XML-RPC error:
   ```bash
   grep -E '^display_errors' /etc/php/8.5/*/php.ini
   ```
2. The web server user must be in `mtagroup`, because the quarantine directories are `drwxrwx--- postfix mtagroup`. MailScanner's installer doesn't add it:
   ```bash
   id www-data
   usermod -a -G mtagroup www-data
   systemctl restart apache2
   ```
   If PHP runs under php-fpm, check the pool user and restart `php8.5-fpm`.

title: Add a check script for the deploy log classifier (cron could_not_set cases)
body:
## What

Add a reusable check for the deploy log classifier, `classify_log()` / `classify_new_log()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`. It decides which new web PHP log lines are WordPress's cron `could_not_set` notice (a warning) and which fail an install, and it has changed in three releases running (GH#639, GH#658, GH#666). Each time the cases were checked with a throwaway script; a committed one keeps the cases and lets a plugin re-run them after a sync.

## How

- New core script `scripts/check-deploy-log.sh` (name may differ; keep it under `scripts/`, which `.distignore` already keeps out of the zips). Add it to `scripts/core-files.txt` and to `DEVELOPMENT.md` → Checks or Deploying to sites, and to the core-file list `scripts/rename-plugin.sh` relies on if it needs one.
- It sources the library with `DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ONLY=1` (as `RELEASING.md` documents for fleet scripts), writes each case to a log file in a `mktemp -d` folder, sets `LOG_FILES`, `LOG_BEFORE=(0)`, `LOG_FIRST=("")`, `LOG_INODE=("$(file_inode "$file")")` and `CRON_HOOKS_RUN`, calls `classify_new_log` and compares `LOG_FAIL`/`LOG_NEW_LINES` with the expected result. One line per case (`ok`/`FAIL`, label, `LOG_WARN`), exit 1 on any mismatch. `--awk PATH` (optional) runs it with another awk by putting it first on `PATH`.
- Cases (timestamp prefix `[09-Nov-2026 02:53:00 UTC] `, JSON `{"schedule":"daily","args":[],"interval":86400}`, hooks run: two plugin hooks):
  - warn: English reschedule and unschedule notices; Dutch (`Cron ongepland event fout voor hook: HOOK, foutcode: could_not_set, foutmelding: …, gegevens: {…}`); French (`… pour le crochet : HOOK, Code d’erreur : could_not_set, Message d’erreur : …, Données : {…}`); German (`Cron-Ereignis-Fehler beim Neuplanen für Hook: …`); no timestamp; Apache format with `[php:notice] [pid …] [client …]` blocks and a trailing `, referer: URL`; another plugin's hook (cron save contention).
  - fail: `Payment task failed for hook: HOOK, status: could_not_set` (own hook, other hook, with trailing `, retry later`); a plugin line with digits before the hook and a four-field tail; `PHP Notice:` and `PHP Fatal error:` lines quoting the notice; `could_not_set_x`; no message/JSON; text after the JSON; a plain PHP warning.
- Shell rules: ShellCheck clean, Bash 3.2 compatible, `local var="$1"`, explicit `return 0`.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `scripts/check-deploy-log.sh`
- EDIT: `scripts/core-files.txt`
- EDIT: `DEVELOPMENT.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `scripts/check-deploy-log.sh` passes with macOS awk; `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo:ro -w /repo debian:bookworm-slim bash scripts/check-deploy-log.sh` passes with mawk (and with GNU Awk after `apt-get install -y gawk`).
- Reverting the GH#666 classifier change (`git show 534551d:scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`) makes the payment-line and `PHP Notice` cases fail the check.
- `scripts/lint.sh shell` passes; `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` has 0 errors.

Follow-up from GH#666 (PR #667, v1.0.55), where these cases were run by hand.

title: deploy-sites.sh --apply: run the plugin's own WP-Cron events after install, so a fatal error only in cron callbacks fails the deploy
body:
## Why

A plugin made from the starter released a version with a fatal error that occurred only in its WP-Cron callbacks on single sites: it called `ms_is_switched()`, which WordPress defines on multisite only (wpallstars/seoprostack#1248). `scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` passed it on every single site:

- the guarded full load (`load_code()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`) loads the plugin but runs none of its scheduled callbacks;
- the home fetch is a front-end request, which never reached that code;
- the PHP log check found nothing, because the host's cron job runs WP-Cron from the command line, where the fatal error goes to the cron job's output, not to the site's PHP error log.

The sites' caches were then never refilled, and cron runs stopped at that event, until a person noticed slow pages half an hour later. CI's smoke tests (single site and multisite) also load the plugin without running its cron callbacks, and PHPStan's WordPress stubs declare multisite-only functions on every site.

## What

After each site's full load in `--apply` (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, next to `load_code()`), run the plugin's own scheduled events once on that site, for example `wp cron event run <hooks>` for the hooks starting with `{prefix}_` that `wp cron event list --fields=hook` lists (in this process, `launch => false`, as the purge does). Fail the install, with its restore command, when one ends in a PHP fatal error or a non-zero exit. Print `cron=N/M` on the install line.

Points for the implementer to settle:

- Time: a plugin's event may run for long (a cache fill can take up to 90 seconds from the command line). Consider a time limit per event, or a `{prefix}_deploy_smoke` action that a plugin can use to call the cheap paths of its cron work instead, with the hook run as a fallback.
- Side effects: running an event early also reschedules it, the same as `wp cron event run` by hand; say so in `RELEASING.md` step 5.
- Networks: per site, as the full load is.

Optionally, the same step in the CI smoke test (`.github/workflows/`), single site and multisite, so a fatal error like this fails the pull request before release.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (`load_code()` and the install line), `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` (usage text), `RELEASING.md` (step 5 and the tools table).
- Possibly the smoke test workflow and its script under `scripts/`.

## Verification

- A plugin build with a cron callback that calls an undefined function: `--apply` on a single-site test install fails with the fatal error and prints the restore command; on a network, likewise per site.
- A normal build: `cron=N/N`, install passes, and the run time grows by no more than the events' own run time.
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.

Then sync to plugins made from the starter with `scripts/sync-core.sh`.
