title: deploy-sites.sh: WordPress cron-save contention notices (could_not_set) mark healthy installs FAIL
body:
## What

`scripts/deploy-sites.sh --apply` marks an install **FAIL** (and prints its restore command) whenever the web PHP log gained any line during the install. During a real multi-site rollout, five installs were marked FAIL whose only new lines were WordPress core's cron-save contention notices, for example:

```
Cron reschedule event error for hook: <plugin>_hourly, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":"hourly","args":[],"interval":3600}
Cron unschedule event error for hook: <plugin>_process, Error code: could_not_set, ...
```

On a site whose admin language is Dutch the same notice was translated (`Cron ongepland event fout voor hook: ..., foutcode: could_not_set, ...`), but the error code `could_not_set` stays in English.

These come from WordPress core (`wp_reschedule_event()` / `wp_unschedule_event()` logging a `could_not_set` WP_Error when `_set_cron_array()` returns false). That happens when two cron runners save the cron option at the same moment: the deploy's own cron run (`cron=N/M`) races ordinary WP-Cron traffic or another plugin's rollout on the same sites. Two of the five FAILs were for another plugin's hook, not the deployed plugin's. After each FAIL the install was healthy: the new version was active, and `wp cron event list` showed every plugin event still scheduled. No restore was needed, but the report told the operator to restore.

## Why

A FAIL with a restore command for a harmless race costs an operator investigation on every rollout to a busy host. It also trains people to ignore FAIL, which hides real fatals.

## Where

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: the new-log-lines count (around `new_lines=0` … `new_lines=$((new_lines + added))`) and the result decision `if [[ "$after" != "$want" || "$new_lines" -gt 0 || "$SITES_FAILED" -gt 0 ]]; then result="FAIL"` (about line 802). `new_log_text` prints the lines.
- `RELEASING.md` (the deploy-sites section describing FAIL and WARN) if it explains which log lines fail an install.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- EDIT: `RELEASING.md` (only if it describes the FAIL rule)

## Do

1. Classify each new log line. A line is cron-save contention when it matches WordPress core's cron error notice with error code `could_not_set`. Match on the untranslated code, for example `could_not_set` together with `Data: {"schedule"` or its translation-safe shape, not on the English message.
2. Count only the other lines towards FAIL. When every new line is cron-save contention, report `WARN cron save contention (N lines)` instead of FAIL, still print the lines, and print no restore command.
3. Optionally, after a contention-only install, confirm the plugin's own events are still scheduled (`wp cron event list`). If one is missing, keep FAIL.
4. Keep everything else unchanged: PHP fatals, warnings, notices and any unrecognised line still FAIL.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes (ShellCheck clean).
- Feed the classifier a log containing only the two English sample lines above plus the Dutch one: the result is WARN, the lines are shown, and there is no restore line.
- Add one `PHP Fatal error:` line to the same log: the result is FAIL with the restore command.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` in a plugin made from the starter shows the updated core file after sync.

title: Keep pages cached: no could_not_set log line when a purge moves the batch during a cron run
body:
## What happens

Sites with **Keep pages cached** on log this line from WordPress's `wp-cron.php` when a cache purge lands during a cron run:

```
Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":false,"args":[]}
```

Measured on our own Hostinger sites (LiteSpeed, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.191, WordPress 7.1.4), counting `could_not_set` lines for this hook in each site's `error_log`: 1 on 8 November, 67 in English on 9 November (plus the same line in Dutch and French, about 70 in all), across 20 sites, after Keep pages cached was turned on for a group of busy multisite networks whose builders purge the cache many times an hour. The other hooks' `could_not_set` lines fell away after #1232: `mwai_tasks_internal_run` had 167 unschedule lines on 5 November, 1 on 8 November and none on 9 November.

## Why (confirmed in code)

1. `wp-cron.php` reads the due events once, at its start.
2. A purge in another request calls `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later()` → `save($queue, DELAY, true)`, which clears the due event and schedules it `DELAY` seconds later, so the fill runs after LiteSpeed applies the purge.
3. `wp-cron.php` then calls `wp_unschedule_event($timestamp, $hook, $args, true)` for the copy it read. `SEOProStack_Cron_List::write()` applies the removal to the stored list, which no longer has the event, so the merged list equals the stored one; the database update changes no rows, `update_option()` returns false, and core logs `could_not_set`.
4. `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::run()` then sees the moved event (`SEOProStack_Cron_List::next_stored()`, #1362) and leaves it to run at its new time. **Nothing is lost**: the line is noise, but it is SEO Pro Stack's noise, it hides real errors, and the deploy check counts it.

The same happens whenever two requests remove the same event (two cron runners that read the same due event).

## Fix

In `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php`, add a `pre_unschedule_event` filter (registered in `init()` beside `write()`): when the event (time, hook, hash of its arguments) is no longer in the list as stored now (`stored()`), it is already unscheduled, so return `true` and drop the option caches as `write()` does when another request already applied a change (#1270), so the rest of the request reads the stored list. When the stored list cannot be read, or still has the event, return the filter's value unchanged and let core remove it.

- Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php` (new filter method, `init()`), `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).
- Pattern: `SEOProStack_Cron_List::write()` and `next_stored()` in the same file.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On the test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): `wp eval` that schedules a single event in the past, reads the list (so the request has its copy), removes the event from the stored `cron` option with a direct database update, then calls `wp_unschedule_event($time, $hook, array(), true)`: before the fix it returns `WP_Error` `could_not_set`; after, `true`, and `wp cron event list` shows no copy of the event. Normal unscheduling (event still stored) still removes it.
- After deploy: no new `could_not_set` lines for `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` in the sites' `error_log` over a day of purges.

title: Deploy check: a cron could_not_set race it caused itself counts as a new log error
body:
## What

During the 1.3.162 rollout, one busy network install (4 sites) was reported as `FAIL` with `new_log_lines=2`. Both lines came from `wp-cron.php` in the same second that the deploy check ran the plugin's events with `wp cron event run` (`run_site_cron()` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`, about line 551):

```
Cron reschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check, Error code: could_not_set, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {"schedule":"seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check","args":[],"interval":300}
Cron unschedule event error for hook: seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check, Error code: could_not_set, ...
```

WordPress logs these when `_set_cron_array()` has nothing to save because another process has just rescheduled the same event. Here the deploy's forced run and the site's own cron runner handled the same five-minute event at once. The plugin only schedules that event when it is missing (`SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::sync_check()`), so the deploy check caused the race; it is not a plugin fault. All four sites loaded, every cron event ran, and every home page answered 200. The install stayed on the new version.

## Fix

When counting new web-log lines, treat `Cron (reschedule|unschedule) event error for hook: <hook>, Error code: could_not_set` as a warning when `<hook>` is one of the hooks `run_site_cron()` has just run (it already has the list). Show it as, for example, `WARN cron race <hook>`. Count every other new line as before.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: `run_site_cron()` and the code that counts `new_log_lines`. This is a core file, so take the change to the starter as well (`STANDARDS.md` → Agent docs; the current drift is #1290).
- `RELEASING.md`, the paragraph on `cron=N/M` (about lines 176-185): mention the race warning.

## Verification

- ShellCheck on `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: no findings.
- Feed the log-counting function a log holding one race line for a hook it ran, one race line for a hook it did not run, and one PHP warning. The first is a warning; the other two fail.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `RELEASING.md`

title: Flaky: ssh lookalike allow-case refused as ssh-to-self in the cron command vet
body:
## Flake

`test/test_mcp_cron_security.py::test_vet_shell_command_allows_smuggling_lookalikes[ssh -o ConnectTimeout=10 backup@host uptime]` failed on Backend Tests (3.12, 3) for #15592 at ad8ff057f (a PR that does not touch `security/` or the command vet):

```
AssertionError: should allow: 'ssh -o ConnectTimeout=10 backup@host uptime'
assert 'Error: cron command blocked by security policy: ... sandbox-escape-ssh-self component=argv-floor ...'
```

The same test passes alone on that head and on main (`PYTHONPATH=src`, run locally).

## Likely cause (not yet confirmed)

`sandbox-escape-ssh-self` decides "self" from a process-wide set of the host's own names (`security/argv_floor.py` ~1942-2233): a `gethostname` seed published on first use, plus DNS-derived names (`getfqdn`/`getaddrinfo`) added by a background enrichment. If another test in the same xdist worker patches `socket.gethostname`/`getfqdn` to `host` (or the runner's own resolver maps a name to `host`) while that set is first built or enriched, the set keeps `host` for the rest of the worker, and this allow-case is then refused as ssh-to-self.

## To do

Confirm by running the file after the tests that patch `socket` hostname functions in one worker; then make the self-host set test-isolated (reset between tests, or keyed so a patched value cannot outlive its test), and give this parametrization a host name that cannot be a self name (e.g. a reserved `.invalid` name).

comments.body:
Fix is up in https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/pull/20861.

The hypothesis in this issue (a test that patches `socket.gethostname` leaving `host` in the self-name set) turned out to be wrong. The cause is a race in production code: on a cold worker the first dotless ssh check parses the hosts file while the own-host enrichment thread publishes the netlink address table and the DNS merge. Each publication moves the hosts-cache key, the parse reports "changed", and the gate answers pending, which the vet refuses as `sandbox-escape-ssh-self`. On current main a cold call with a 20 ms parse is refused in 19 of 20 runs. The PR makes `_hosts_file_verdict` judge the file again on the new key, up to three times, before answering pending.

Thanks for the report. This issue has been triaged by Crew Captain and will be assigned to a maintainer, who will follow up here.

<!-- kc-triaged -->

Seen again on #17684 at `6bf633dd7`, Backend Tests (3.12, 3): `test_mcp_cron_security.py::test_vet_shell_command_allows_smuggling_lookalikes[ssh -o ConnectTimeout=10 backup@host uptime]` failed with "should allow". That PR does not touch `security/argv_floor.py`. The fix is in #20861, which needs a maintainer to take over its Sensitive Change Review.

Claimed: a worker is picking this up to find why the ssh lookalike allow-case is sometimes refused as ssh-to-self in the cron command vet when run in the full shard. A PR or findings will be linked here.

Findings: this flake is already fixed on `main`. No new PR is needed.

The cause is not a test leaking state. It is a race in the ssh-to-self floor. The first ssh-family vet in a fresh worker starts the own-host thread. That thread publishes while `/etc/hosts` is still being parsed. The hosts cache key moves, and the vet refused the command as `sandbox-escape-ssh-self`.

title: Lane host side: SSH channel with host-key pinning, workload account, candidate and guest file transfer (REQ-106)
body:
## Objective

Implement the host side of the lane's guest channel, so the engine can reach a fresh lane instance and hand it everything the guest supervisor merged under #204 (`scripts/lane/supervisor.py`) needs:
- an SSH connection that accepts only the box receipt's host key;
- the runner-unit check and tool probes;
- the candidate commit and the guest files;
- the output disk's device path.

Like #202 and #204, this slice is offline-testable. Argv construction and each step's checks run against injected `run`, file, and clock functions, and nothing starts a VM.

## Current state (`develop` `5ed0aab`, PR #205)

- `plan.py` plans these `prepare` steps as `engine` steps with no argv: `connect`, `check-runner-units`, `transfer-candidate`. It also plans `verify-instance` (`VBoxManage showvminfo {uuid} --machinereadable`) and `probe-<tool>` (60 s).
- The plan keeps the receipt's `sshHostKey` (`ssh-ed25519`) and the SSH forward from `127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- The generated Vagrantfile sets `config.vm.communicator = "none"`, so Vagrant never connects and never inserts a client key.
- `supervisor.py` expects these in `/run/projectbuddy-lane`, all owned by root:
  - the directory itself, mode `0755`;
  - `supervisor.py`, `output_disk.py`, and `lane-guest.json` (`projectbuddy/lane-guest@1`), mode `0644`;
  - `secrets`, mode `0600`, holding one `NAME=VALUE\0` per declared secret in declared order, and empty when none is declared.
- The spec's `account`, `root`, and `device` are not produced anywhere yet.
- `plan.output_device(uuid)` maps the output VDI's medium UUID to `/dev/disk/by-id/ata-VBOX_HARDDISK_VB…` (`DevAHCI.cpp` serial format, verified on #204).

## Decisions (each has a recommendation)

1. **SSH client credential and login account.** Nothing in the lane or the lane box defines which key or account the engine logs in with, and no file in the repository provisions an `authorized_keys`.
   - **Recommended:** research what the base bootstrap and box packaging leave in the guest first. Then pick one of two:
     - a per-run ed25519 client key generated on the host in the run directory (mode `0600`, deleted by teardown) and authorized in the guest in a way the receipt can attest; or
     - a key the box receipt already names.
   - Rejected: Vagrant's insecure key, and any password login.
2. **Workload account.** The steps must not run as the SSH login account. A step that can write that account's dotfiles or `authorized_keys` could hijack a later root session over SSH, such as `start-build`.
   - **Recommended:** the engine creates a dedicated account at run time during `prepare`, as root over SSH, for example `useradd --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin pb-workload`. It has a locked password, no sudo, and no SSH keys, and is listed in `/etc/cron.deny` and `/etc/at.deny`. This also closes the cron/at residual risk recorded on #204.
   - Creating the account per run needs no box repackaging, because every instance is a fresh clone.
   - Refuse if the account already exists.
3. **Candidate transfer.**
   - **Recommended:** `git archive --format=tar <commit>` on the host, streamed over SSH into `root` and unpacked as the workload account with `tar --no-same-owner --no-same-permissions`. `root` is the account's home `candidate/` directory plus the declaration's `workingDirectory`.
   - Record the archive's SHA-256 for the REQ-092 evidence record.
   - Alternative: a `git bundle` with the commit only, if a consumer's build needs Git metadata. Settle this against the challenge workload's `npm run package`.
4. **Guest file placement.**
   - **Recommended:** as root over SSH, `install -d -m 0755 -o root -g root /run/projectbuddy-lane`. Refuse if it already exists.
   - Place the three `0644` files, then write `secrets` through `install -m 0600 /dev/stdin`, so no secret value is ever in argv. Write `secrets` last and only while the link is on, immediately before `start-build`.
   - Verify each placed file's SHA-256 in the guest against the

## Design (research done; recommended options taken under standing approval)

### Research findings

- **The base VM has one login, a password.**
  - `build-virtualbox.sh` runs VirtualBox's unattended install, which creates `GUEST_USER` (default `actor`) from the operator's password file.
  - `base-bootstrap.sh` installs `openssh-server` with Ubuntu's defaults: password login is accepted, and root login is `prohibit-password`.
  - The appliance tooling logs in with that password: `complete-public-provisioning.py` uses `SSH_ASKPASS` and `sudo` with the password on stdin. Step 4 of the lane box procedure collects evidence with `ssh $GUEST_USER@127.0.0.1 sudo cat`.
- **Nothing in the lane box changes that.** `install-toolchain`, `readiness`, and the packager touch neither accounts nor sshd, and no file provisions an `authorized_keys`. A packaged lane box would therefore carry a password login known to whoever built it.
- **Guest properties already cross the boundary on this base.** `base-bootstrap.sh` publishes the host-key fingerprint with `VBoxControl guestproperty set`. `VBoxControl` comes from `virtualbox-guest-utils`.
- **VirtualBox sources (trunk):**
  - `VBoxManage guestproperty set <vm> <name> <value> --flags <flags>` takes `--flags` as a separate fifth argument (`VBoxManageGuestProp.cpp`, `handleSetGuestProperty`).
  - `VBoxControl guestproperty get <name> --verbose` prints `Value:`, `Timestamp:`, and `Flags:` lines. With no value set it prints `No value set!` and exits

**PR A (box side) is open: #209.** Implementing it refined the design posted above in four ways. Each is backed by offline evidence against the noble packages.

1. **The unit is ordered `Before=ssh.service` only, not `ssh.socket`.** A service with default dependencies that is ordered before a socket forms a cycle, because `sockets.target` comes before `basic.target`. The base bootstrap enables `ssh.service` (`base-bootstrap.sh`), not the socket. Until the key file exists, every login fails closed, so the host channel (PR B) must poll for SSH rather than assume it is ready at first connect.
2. **`VBoxControl` is at `/usr/sbin/VBoxControl`** on noble (`virtualbox-guest-utils 7.0.16-dfsg-2ubuntu1.3`), not `/usr/bin`. The noble `virtualbox-guest-utils.service` is `Type=forking`, `ConditionVirtualization=oracle`, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`. Flags are formatted host-side: `RDONLYGUEST` alone prints `RDONLYGUEST`, and together with `RDONLYHOST` it prints `READONLY`. The helper accepts either.
3. **The readiness attestation runs `sshd -T -C user=<u>,host=10.0.2.2,addr=10.0.2.2`**, the NAT source address, rather than `host=lane`. It runs for root and for every account whose shell is not a nologin/false shell, and checks 15 settings. With a hostile `50-cloud-init.conf` (passwords on, root login on, `.ssh/authorized_keys`), noble sshd 9.6 still prints exactly the drop-in's values. A `Match User` override or an appended `AllowUsers` shows up in that account's output, so readiness catch

The design above used `/ProjectBuddy/Lane/ClientKey` and relied on the `RDONLYGUEST` flag to prove that the host set it. That does not hold. In `VBoxGuestPropSvc.cpp` (v7.0.0, v7.1.0, v7.2.6, and trunk), `setPropertyInternal` checks permission against the existing property's flags, or against no flags when the property doesn't exist yet. A guest process (root or not; the service ignores who in the guest calls) could therefore run `VBoxControl guestproperty set /ProjectBuddy/Lane/ClientKey "<its key>" --flags RDONLYGUEST`. The property would persist in the VM config, and at a later boot with no host-set key, the helper would have accepted it.

**Fix (pushed to #209):** the property is now `/VirtualBox/HostInfo/ProjectBuddy/Lane/ClientKey`.
- `checkHostReserved` refuses every guest set under `/VirtualBox/HostInfo/`, whether the property exists or not.
- When the host sets such a name, VirtualBox ORs in `RDONLYGUEST`. This includes the bulk load of stored properties at VM start (`VMMDevInterface.cpp` → `i_guestPropSetMultiple`).
- A guest delete of a host-set value is refused, because the flag is set.
- The helper's flag check stays as a second layer.
- A test pins the reserved prefix (mutation-checked).

## PR B design: the host side of the access channel

Taken under standing approval: my recommended option for each decision, recorded here before the code.

PR B is split into two PRs, so each one gets a focused review:

| Slice | Steps | Scope |

| **B1: host channel** | `client-key`, `connect`, `check-runner-units` | the run's client key and how it reaches the guest; host-key enrollment; the hardened `ssh` argv; the runner-unit refusal |

### B1 decisions

**H1: key delivery.** A new engine step, `client-key`, is the first `prepare` step:
- It runs `ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N "" -C <instance> -f <run dir>/client-key`. It refuses if either key file already exists, and checks the public key's form and blob.
- The generated Vagrantfile adds `vb.customize ["guestproperty", "set", :id, "/VirtualBox/HostInfo/ProjectBuddy/Lane/ClientKey", File.read('<run dir>/client-key.pub').chomp, "--flags", "RDONLYGUEST"]` after the output-disk lines. Vagrant runs it pre-boot on the imported clone.

**PR B1 merged:** VITechnologies/projectbuddy#212, merge commit `76b96fe` (head `f33e5ab`).

The workload placement steps are in `scripts/lane/placement.py`. Each runs as root over the SSH channel, checks every command's exit code, and stops the run unless the guest ends in the state the step checks for:

title: bug: opnsense provider rejects system.*, radvd and cron.jobs resource types
body:
> Originally issue #1144 by @​endavis, opened 2026-10-27.
> Closed 2026-10-27 (completed).

## Bug Description

The OPNsense provider registers component managers for `system.hostname`, `system.dns`, `system.ssh`, `system.webgui`, `system.firmware`, `system.remotebackup`, `system.tuning`, `radvd` and `cron.jobs` (`providers/opnsense/__init__.py`, the manager table around line 262). But `get_resource_types()` (around line 428) doesn't list them. `Orchestrator.validate_resources` (`core/orchestrator.py:390`) rejects any type not in that list before a manager runs, so none of those types can be planned or applied.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add to an environment's OPNsense YAML:
   ```yaml
   opnsense:
     system:
       dns:
         dns_servers: [172.20.10.1]
   ```
2. Run `uv run foundry infra plan --env fw-test` (main at a2c3f7d):
   ```
   ValueError: Provider 'opnsense' does not support resource type 'system.dns' for resource 'settings'. Supported types: firewall.rules, interfaces.vlans, ...
   ```

## Expected vs Actual Behavior

- **Expected:** every type with a registered manager and a loader shape (`DOTTED_RESOURCE_SHAPES`) is accepted.
- **Actual:** only the 15 types in `get_resource_types()` are; the others are rejected.

## Additional Context

- Fix: derive `get_resource_types()` from the manager table, or add the missing types, and add a test that every manager key is a supported type, so the lists can't drift again.
- Each type's `get_dependencies()` entry should be checked at the same time.

实现规格：[`docs/spec-backend.md`](https://github.com/sishoui/model-light/blob/master/docs/spec-backend.md)，§7 / §10 / §12。

## What to build

一台自己的服务器上，`docker compose up -d` 就把整套跑起来：MySQL + api + Caddy 自动 HTTPS，

- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` 三个服务（db / api / caddy），`db` 带 healthcheck，`api` 等 db healthy 再起

      回滚 = 镜像退回上一 tag + 必要时快照恢复
- [ ] 每日 `mysqldump` + cron，保留 14 天
- [ ] 日志保留 7 天，超期自动清理；不打印 openid / token / arrangement

title: [T-301][P0][M3] Bezpieczny ekstraktor SQL/JSONL z jawnie ograniczoną gramatyką
body:
# Bezpieczny ekstraktor SQL/JSONL z jawnie ograniczoną gramatyką

Cel: poprawić obecne `iter_insert_rows` i `scan_database` (obecnie wczytują SQL do RAM i rozpoznają tylko podzbiór).
Zakres:
- strumieniowe parsowanie obsługiwanego podzbioru mysqldump/MariaDB; zmienne prefiksy; escaped quotes; wielowierszowe INSERT; granice zasobów.
- JSONLDBAdapter ze ścisłą walidacją; role w usermeta, options/cron, tylko obsługiwane formaty.
- nieznane statementy, częściowe rekordy, błędny encoding jako `coverage_gaps`; nigdy nie uruchamiać surowego SQL.
- wyraźna polityka PHP serialized data jako bezpiecznego parsowania danych, bez instancjonowania obiektów.
DoD: testy fuzz/negative, pliki wielkości granicznej, brak fałszywych alarmów „nowy admin” bez baseline.
Zależność: T-101, T-102.

## Zasady wspólne
- Pracuj na osobnej gałęzi, mały PR, bez push/merge do main bez przeglądu.
- Dołącz testy pozytywne i negatywne, wynik komend, listę znanych luk, ryzyka, wpływ na coverage i rollback.
- Tylko syntetyczne fixtures; brak autentycznych backupów, haseł, tokenów i danych osobowych.
- Przestrzegaj `docs/WPTrace_Specyfikacja_Senior_PoC_2026-11-09.md`.

comments.body: Uwaga do zakresu T-301: wykrywanie pominiętych instrukcji (PR #20–#23) to heurystyka nałożona na parser PoC. Kolejne przeglądy znajdowały rozbieżności z prawdziwym parserem MySQL (instrukcja po średniku, komentarze wykonywalne, `DELIMITER`, polecenia klienta). Docelowo parser strumieniowy powinien działać w trybie ścisłym: każdy bajt zrzutu należy do rozpoznanej instrukcji albo powstaje luka — bez osobnego detektora.

Stan T-301 po PR #37–#44. Wszystkie PR-y są scalone, CI zielone.

- **#37:** podział kodu bazy na moduły (ADR 0006).
- **#38:** reguły bazy: role z kluczy tablicy uprawnień (dane serializowane PHP czytane jako dane, obiekty są nieprzezroczyste), prefiks tabel ze zrzutu, inwentarz administratorów/cron/wtyczek, `NEW_SINCE_BASELINE`, cytat z redakcją.
- **#39:** ścisły parser strumieniowy zrzutu SQL. Porcje pochodzą z odczytu SecureIngest, w którym liczony jest SHA-256; limit 20 MiB zniknął.
- **#40:** adapter JSONL i `--database-format`.
- **#41:** dokumentacja M3 i odświeżone demo.
- **#42, #44:** utwardzenie po dwóch przeglądach bezpieczeństwa (agent i automatyczny przegląd commita): zapis ukryty w instrukcjach obojętnych i komentarzach wykonywalnych, różnice leksera względem serwera (`--`, `sql_mode`, kodowanie), wiązanie kolumn, nazwy różniące się wielkością liter, limity pamięci.

DoD według oceny agenta, wyłącznie na danych syntetycznych:
- fuzz (mutacje z ustalonym ziarnem) i testy negatywne;
- pliki graniczne (21 MiB, instrukcja ponad 16 MiB, limit pliku);
- brak ustalenia „nowy admin” bez zaufanej listy.

macOS: 2496 passed, 5 skipped, 2 xfailed.

Otwarte:
- zgodność z rzeczywistymi zrzutami `mysqldump`/`mariadb-dump` niezmierzona;
- WP-DB-002/004/005/006 poza zakresem;
- przegląd człowieka zmian w `ingest.py` (`sink`) i w parserze wymagany przed bramką GO/NO-GO.

Issue zostawiam otwarte do decyzji właściciela.

M3 domknięte: kod i dokumentacja scalone (PR #37–#45), CI zielone na `main`. DoD z Issue spełnione na danych syntetycznych. Otwarte ograniczenia (zgodność z rzeczywistym mysqldump/mariadb-dump niezmierzona, brak limitu czasu w trakcie pliku SQL/JSONL, WP-DB-002/004/005/006 brak, wymagany przegląd człowieka parsera `sqldump.py`, `jsonldb.py` i zmian w `ingest.py`) są opisane w `docs/PROGRESS.md` i ADR 0006.

title: V6.1 maintenance: reliable automatic database backup (no server changes)
body:
## Incident and accepted outcome
Owner's operational AChBot has otherwise continued working, but automatic Telegram database backup has failed since approximately V5 deployment. Live read-only aaPanel diagnostics established four registered Cron wrappers running aaPanel PHP 8.1 with `PATH` assignments excluding `/www/server/mysql/bin`; `/usr/bin/mysqldump` missing while `/www/server/mysql/bin/mysqldump` is executable. SQL file was zero bytes; ZIP absent; `setting.LAST_BACKUP_TIME` advanced despite failure. See Issue #14 investigative comments (especially #issuecomment-6127565579).

**Owner's explicit constraint:** Do NOT change the operational server, existing working bot, system PHP/MySQL/Cron/PATH, real DB, permissions or live configuration. Fix **only the AChBot source** on an isolated development branch, perform all tests on authorized disposable infrastructure, produce a reviewable PR. No merge, release, deployment, operational test or production data access without separate owner authorization.

## Required coherent fix
1. Self-contained `mysqldump` discovery: support aaPanel absolute MariaDB location, common system locations and safe explicit override; never assume inherited Cron `PATH`.
2. Fail closed and visibly (credential-redacted diagnostics) on missing/unexecutable dump utility, nonzero dump exit, empty/invalid SQL, ZIP failure or Telegram upload failure. Keep SQL dump contents/private DB credentials out of HTTP webroot; use only restrictive temporary files and guaranteed normal cleanup.
3. Preserve `settings/rewardReport.php` name, expected schedule duration, Telegram caption/document contract, unchanged MariaDB schema, webhook/panels/bot financial logic. Next-due timestamp advances **only when backup delivery succeeds**, not merely when attempted. Prevent simultaneous duplicate backup execution from multiple Cron wrappers for the same app.
4. Include synthetic failure/success/negative/concurrency tests, isolated real MariaDB dump/ZIP/Telegram acceptance where feasible, source-boundary regression, complete audited source-only ZIP manifest and exact-candidate CI; no real tokens, payments, Telegram send or production access.
5. Publish one cohesive PR with evidence. Author-separated independent review and explicit owner integration/release/deployment gates, no claim of operator PASS.

## Provenance
Original V0–V6 `sendDatabaseBackup()` body unchanged; original scheduler unchanged. Legacy unqualified dump binary and error suppression predate V5; incident is environmental/compatibility break surfaced on owner's host, not a proven V5 source regression. Fix is an intentionally behavior-correcting separate scope outside parity requirements.

```sh
wp mg-saoluu backup --components=database --reason=pre-deploy --ref=<FULL_GIT_SHA> --format=json
wp mg-saoluu list --format=json
wp mg-saoluu verify --id=<BACKUP_ID> --format=json
```

Rules:
- Register under `WP_CLI` only. No REST endpoint and no HTTP actions.
- `backup` allows only `database` in P2A; reject unsupported scopes/values.
- `--ref` must be the **full** hexadecimal Git commit SHA, not a short SHA or `latest`. This ref is a traceability label, **not a complete multi-repo release manifest**; P3 must bind per-component repo + full SHA.
- JSON stdout: one parseable object, stable keys such as `ok`, `backup_id`, `scope`, `git_ref`, `archive_sha256`, `created_at`, `error_code`; errors/details to stderr without secrets. Exit `0` only on complete verified success; nonzero otherwise.
- `list` does not mutate application tables; list recognizable archive IDs/types/dates and verification state, including DB-only checkpoints.
- `verify --id` only reads the identified allowed backup and checks ZIP structure, manifest, SQL hash and finished-archive SHA-256; reject path traversal/symlink/missing/altered files. Differentiate `archive_verified` from `restore_drill_pass`.
- Keep archive ZIP format v1.3.1 compatible; do not introduce a new package format.

## Reuse existing code, do NOT rewrite engine

Existing `mg_saoluu_create_backup('sql', ...)` runs `mg_saoluu_run_mysqldump()` with `--single-transaction --quick --skip-lock-tables`, packs `database_backup.sql` into ZIP, writes manifest/payload hashes, final archive hash, and private metadata.

P2A may make a **small shared service/CLI adapter** but must not duplicate the SQL dump, ZIP hash, storage, or catalog logic.

CLI must take the existing non-blocking operation lock (or shared backup entrypoint with equivalent lock), release it in all outcomes, and fail closed on contention. Avoid polling loops.

Checkpoint metadata should bind:
- `reason=pre-deploy`
- exact `git_ref`
- `backup_id`, archive SHA-256, SQL SHA-256, UTC timestamp
- verification status, WordPress DB prefix
- retention/protection state

P2A checkpoints must **not** be pruned by ordinary SQL backup retention while needed for a deployment rollback window. Prefer explicit protected metadata; leave bounded post-deploy cleanup policy to P5, and make disk quota preflight fail closed.

## Database coverage & consistency

- Dump must include every relevant table **present in the connected database**, including WordPress core, WooCommerce, Woo HPOS, MG-OS and other plugin tables when present; do not infer table coverage only from `wp_` prefix.
- Test that the archive is restored with equivalent schema and representative records on an isolated clone, including alternate-prefix fixtures and tables that use custom prefixes.
- Record actual storage-engine inventory (`InnoDB`, `MyISAM`, `MEMORY`, etc.) in P1/QA evidence. MySQL `--single-transaction` only guarantees consistent reads for transactional tables; unsafe/nontransactional mutable tables or concurrent DDL => fail closed / blocker. Do not silently claim transactional consistency for unsupported engines.
- Check operational output for no SQL/table content leaks, credentials, PII or absolute secrets.
- Backup may update **its own private metadata/audit log** but must not intentionally update/delete WordPress/Woo/MG-OS application rows, invoke migrations, or cha

title: infra: backups demostrados + auditoría continua de dependencias (V 0.1.20)
body:
## Backups/restauración demostrada

- \`scripts/backup-database.sh\`: dump comprimido con timestamp y retención (mysqldump/mariadb-dump), pensado para cron en Hostinger igual que \`post-deploy.sh\` (#144).
- \`scripts/verify-backup-restore.sh\`: restaura el dump en una base descartable y confirma que quedó consultable — no es "confiamos en que funciona", se demuestra.
- Nuevo job de CI \`backup-restore\`: en cada corrida con cambios de backend, migra un esquema real, lo respalda y demuestra la restauración end-to-end contra el servicio MariaDB de CI.

## Seguridad continua

- \`composer audit\` y \`npm audit --audit-level=high\` como gates nuevos en CI — auditoría de vulnerabilidades conocidas en cada PR, no una revisión manual esporádica.

## Qué NO incluye (alcance honesto)

- **Performance/capacidad**: no se tocó en este PR — es un frente aparte (deferred).
- Backup automático corriendo en producción vía cron — el script está listo pero activar el cron en Hostinger requiere que un humano lo configure (mismo patrón que #144).
- Backup con destino externo (S3/Drive) — solo local por ahora.
